bubble-ghost: Bubble Ghost is a late-1980s computer puzzle about puffing a bubble through a room of candles and fans. The Game Boy cartridge is a later port of that ghostly blower.
colin-mcrae-rally-1998: Codemasters' Colin McRae Rally (1998) is a stage-based rally game built around the real Scottish driver. The PlayStation original is the known version; a Game Boy edition is a separate, smaller port.
hugo-1991: Hugo (1991) stars the troll from ITE's interactive television quizzes, a character Scandinavian kids played through their TV remotes. Later cartridges, including a Game Boy one, turned those show tasks into a handheld product.
bugs-life-a: Disney•Pixar A Bug's Life licenses the 1998 Pixar film. The Nintendo 64 platformer and the Game Boy versions are different games that share the movie's insects.
kirbys-dream-land-2-1995: HAL's Kirby's Dream Land 2 (1995) is the Game Boy sequel that pairs Kirby with animal friends, including a hamster, an owl, and a fish. It sits between the first Game Boy Kirby and the Super Nintendo Dream Land 3.
asteroids-1979: Atari's Asteroids (1979), by Lyle Rains and Ed Logg, is the vector-arcade game of a ship turning and thrusting among rocks. Later handheld versions are ports; the cabinet is the original.
pokemon-yellow-version-special-pikachu-e: Game Freak's Pokémon Yellow Version: Special Pikachu Edition, released in Japan in 1998, keeps Pikachu at your side and follows the anime more closely than Red and Green. It is a special edition of the first generation, not a new region.
missile-command: Dave Theurer's Missile Command is Atari's 1980 arcade game of defending cities from falling warheads. The trackball cabinet is the famous version; a Game Boy release years later does not make it a handheld original.
disneys-pocahontas: Disney's Pocahontas is a Game Boy tie-in to Disney's animated film, one of several licensed Pocahontas games from the mid-1990s. It is not a major 16-bit platformer on the scale of Aladdin or The Lion King.
road-rash-old: Electronic Arts' Road Rash (1991) is the Genesis motorcycle racer where you punch other riders and dodge the police. That 16-bit game is the series identity; Game Boy versions are later, smaller offshoots.
the-king-of-fighters-96: SNK's The King of Fighters '96 is the Neo Geo team tournament that changes bosses and lineups after the previous year's entry. A Game Boy port exists, but the arcade version is the real annual release.
breakout-1976: Atari's Breakout (1976) clears a brick wall with a ball and paddle, and Steve Wozniak's prototype for the company is part of its origin story. Any Game Boy edition is a distant port of that arcade idea.
the-king-of-fighters-95: SNK's The King of Fighters '95 is the team-based sequel to the first King of Fighters on Neo Geo. The Game Boy version is a reduced portable conversion of that 1995 arcade game.
castlevania-ii-belmonts-revenge: Konami's Castlevania II: Belmont's Revenge is the 1991 Game Boy sequel to Castlevania: The Adventure. Christopher Belmont climbs four castles; it is not a portable copy of Simon's Quest.
castlevania-the-adventure-1989: Konami's first handheld Castlevania, Castlevania: The Adventure (1989), is a stiff whip-platform trek that longtime fans still rank as the series' roughest start.
final-fantasy-adventure: Before the Mana series carried that name, Final Fantasy Adventure was Square's 1991 Game Boy action RPG, released in Japan as Seiken Densetsu.
missile-command-1980: Dave Theurer's arcade classic Missile Command (1980) makes you shield cities from falling warheads with a limited stock of interceptors. Atari's trackball cabinet is the game that name means.
r-type-1987: Irem's side-scroller R-Type (1987) is remembered for the Force, a detachable pod that both shields the ship and powers its shot. The arcade cabinet came first; home versions followed.
centipede-1981: Ed Logg and Dona Bailey designed Atari's Centipede (1981), a trackball shooter set in a mushroom patch where the insect splits as you hit it.
battlezone-1980: Ed Rotberg's first-person tank duel Battlezone (1980) drew wireframe enemies on a vector screen. Atari's cabinet was notable enough that the U.S. Army asked about a training variant.
f-1-race: HAL Laboratory built F-1 Race for Nintendo's Famicom in 1984, and it was among the first games to use the console's expansion port for a steering wheel.
new-ghostbusters-ii: HAL Laboratory's New Ghostbusters II is a 1990 license of the film sequel, issued on the NES in Europe and on Game Boy. North America did not receive this cartridge under that title.
donkey-kong-land: Rare's Donkey Kong Land is a 1995 Game Boy companion to Donkey Kong Country, with its own stages squeezed out of pre-rendered artwork. It is a separate trek from the Super Nintendo game.
burgertime-1982: Data East's BurgerTime (1982) stars chef Peter Pepper, who walks across ingredients to stack burgers while kitchen pests chase him across the ladders.
snow-bros: Toaplan's snowball arcade game reached the Game Boy as Snow Bros. Jr. You roll foes into giant snowballs and kick them, a 1990 cabinet idea cut down for a cartridge.
boulder-dash-1984: Peter Liepa's cave puzzle Boulder Dash (1984) has you dig for diamonds while loose boulders tumble. First Star's original spawned a long line of home ports.
real-bout-fatal-fury-special: SNK's Real Bout Fatal Fury Special is a 1997 Neo Geo revision in the Fatal Fury line, tuned as an arcade fighter with the series' plane-switching scraps.
super-star-wars-return-of-the-jedi: Sculptured Software and LucasArts closed the 16-bit trilogy with Super Star Wars: Return of the Jedi, a 1994 Super Nintendo run that includes speeder and Falcon stages.
teenage-mutant-ninja-turtles-fall-of-the: Konami's Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Fall of the Foot Clan is the turtles' 1990 Game Boy debut, a short side-scroller about reaching April. The handheld follow-up is Back from the Sewers.
true-lies: True Lies is an action license of James Cameron's 1994 spy film. Home editions, Game Boy among them, each adapt the movie on their own terms.
lemmings-2-the-tribes: DMA Design's sequel Lemmings 2: The Tribes splits the marchers into tribes with different skills. The 1993 puzzle still asks you to save a set quota of them.
the-lost-world-jurassic-park: Several unrelated 1997 products share the name The Lost World: Jurassic Park, from a Sega light-gun arcade cabinet to separate home adaptations of Spielberg's sequel.
tetris-attack: Nintendo sold Panel de Pon in the West as Tetris Attack, a rising-stack match puzzle restyled around Yoshi. Despite the name, tetrominoes never fall.
casper: The friendly-ghost film spawned Casper, with separate Game Boy and Game Boy Color cartridges in the years after the movie. They are licensed adaptations, not one shared quest.
bonks-adventure: Hudson Soft's PC Engine mascot, also called PC Genjin, debuts in Bonk's Adventure (1989). A Game Boy port came after the TurboGrafx-16 original.
double-dribble-1987: Konami's basketball game Double Dribble (1987) cuts to a close-up dunk when a shot drops. That spectacle, on the arcade cabinet and the NES, became the signature.
battle-arena-toshinden: Tamsoft's weapons fighter Battle Arena Toshinden arrived with the early PlayStation in 1995, published by Takara. Blade duels in 3D, not a handheld scuffle, are what the name refers to.
zen-the-intergalactic-ninja: Konami published Zen: Intergalactic Ninja on Game Boy in 1993, a side-scroller drawn from the small-press comic about an alien warrior.
gargoyles-quest: Capcom's Gargoyle's Quest (1990) stars Firebrand, the red demon from Ghosts 'n Goblins, on a Game Boy map of side-view fights. It is a spinoff, not a Belmont story.
pinocchio-1996: Disney's animated film about the puppet became the license for Pinocchio (1996). Home versions, Game Boy included, each retell that story in their own way.
zool: Gremlin Graphics pitched Zool as a 1992 Amiga mascot, a ninja from the Nth dimension racing through themed worlds. Console and Game Boy ports followed.
bionic-commando-1987: Capcom's arcade original Bionic Commando (1987) introduced the grappling-arm commando that the NES game, where he cannot jump, made famous. A later handheld cartridge reused the name for a different release.
star-wars-1983: Atari's vector cabinet Star Wars (1983) seats you in an X-wing for the Death Star trench. It is a film-based arcade game, built years before the side-scrolling home licenses.
chuck-rock: Core Design's caveman Chuck Rock belly-slams through a 1991 Amiga platformer. Console ports, and a Game Boy version, carried the same prehistoric joke.
fifa-1993: EA's first game in the long soccer line, known in full as FIFA International Soccer, is the release filed as FIFA (1993). Its isometric pitch defined early 16-bit FIFA.
donald-in-maui-mallard: Europe's name for Disney's 1995 platformer is Donald in Maui Mallard. North America called the console versions Maui Mallard in Cold Shadow, with Donald as a shirt-wearing detective.
teenage-mutant-ninja-turtles-ii-back-fro: Konami followed Fall of the Foot Clan with Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles II: Back from the Sewers, a 1991 Game Boy side-scroller that sends the turtles back through the sewers.
xenon-2-megablast: The Bitmap Brothers followed Xenon with Xenon 2: Megablast, a vertical shooter whose soundtrack came from Bomb the Bass. The Amiga original was ported widely, Game Boy included.
mega-man-dr-wilys-revenge: Capcom's first Game Boy Mega Man, Mega Man: Dr. Wily's Revenge, remixes robot masters from the first two NES games. The 1991 cartridge is its own adventure.
gauntlet-ii: Atari Games' 1986 arcade sequel Gauntlet II adds the cursed food called It, plus new classes, to the four-player dungeon crawl.
krustys-fun-house: Audiogenic designed Krusty's Fun House for Acclaim in 1992: herd rats into a machine inside the clown's fun house. The Simpsons puzzle shipped on NES, Super Nintendo, Genesis, and Game Boy.
castlevania-legends: Konami's 1997 Game Boy game Castlevania Legends stars Sonia Belmont. Koji Igarashi later placed this story outside the series timeline he treated as official.
klax: Dave Akers designed Klax for Atari Games in 1989: catch colored tiles from a conveyor and stack them into scoring lines. Ports reached almost every home format of the period.
james-pond-2-codename-robocod: Millennium's fish agent stretches through a toy factory in James Pond 2: Codename Robocod, wearing a robotic suit. It is the sequel to James Pond and a staple of Amiga and console play.
gremlins-2-the-new-batch: Sunsoft's license of Joe Dante's film sequel is Gremlins 2: The New Batch, with separate NES and Game Boy cartridges from 1990. The two versions do not play alike.
super-dodgeball: Technos turned its Kunio arcade dodgeball into Super Dodge Ball (1988), a cult NES sports game full of super throws. The Famicom original sits in the same late-1980s window as the year on this name.
dragon-warrior-monsters: Enix's 1998 Game Boy spinoff Dragon Quest Monsters reached the West as Dragon Warrior Monsters. Breeding and battling creatures is the loop, a pocket cousin of the main series.
the-blues-brothers: Titus built The Blues Brothers in 1991 as a platformer about the Belushi and Aykroyd revue. Computer, console, and Game Boy editions share the license.
marios-picross: Jupiter and Nintendo's Mario's Picross is a 1995 Game Boy logic book: fill grids from number clues while Mario hosts. Japan and Europe got it; North America waited on later reissues.
bubsy-2: Accolade's sequel Bubsy 2 put the bobcat back on Super Nintendo and Genesis in 1994. Larger stages and the same talkative mascot define that follow-up.
yoshis-cookie: Bullet-Proof Software, Nintendo's Tetris partner, co-made Yoshi's Cookie in 1992. Matching cookies in rows on Game Boy and NES clears the board.
mighty-morphin-power-rangers-the-movie: Bandai's Game Boy tie-in to the Rangers feature is titled Mighty Morphin Power Rangers: The Movie (BG). The 1995 movie license is a side-scroller of its own, apart from the TV-season cartridges.
super-off-road: Leland's 1989 arcade racer Super Off Road puts three trucks on an overhead dirt oval under Ivan Stewart's name. A Game Boy port was among the many home versions.
toxic-crusaders: The Troma cartoon spun from The Toxic Avenger licensed Toxic Crusaders in 1992. Bandai's Game Boy cartridge stars those mop-wielding heroes.
the-amazing-spider-man-1990: Rare built LJN's Game Boy release The Amazing Spider-Man (1990) as a side-scroller of wall climbs and street fights. It is the first handheld Spider-Man, separate from the later Super Nintendo and PlayStation games.
kid-icarus-of-myths-and-monsters-2: Nintendo and Tose made Kid Icarus: Of Myths and Monsters for Game Boy in 1991, a sequel to the NES angel-archer. It came out in North America and Europe, and skipped Japan at the time.
final-fantasy-legend-ii: Square's second SaGa game, released in Japan in 1990, is Final Fantasy Legend II in the West. The Game Boy cartridge keeps the mutant, human, and monster party of that line.
turrican: Manfred Trenz's run-and-gun Turrican debuted in 1990 on the Commodore 64 and Amiga, famous for a transforming wheel. A Game Boy port followed the computer original.
the-battle-of-olympus: Infinity's NES action game The Battle of Olympus, published by Broderbund in 1988, sends a Greek hero through side-view fights often compared with Zelda II. A Game Boy port later appeared in Europe.
gargoyles-quest-ii: Capcom moved Firebrand to the NES for Gargoyle's Quest II in 1992, a larger follow-up to the Game Boy original. Japan knew it as Red Arremer II.
speedball-2-brutal-deluxe: The Bitmap Brothers' future sport Speedball 2: Brutal Deluxe is the 1990 Amiga sequel to Speedball, a violent handball match in armor. Ports spread it far beyond that computer.
ultima-old: Richard Garriott's first Britannia role-playing game is what Ultima (Old) points at: the 1981 Apple II original that opened the series.
mega-man-ii: Capcom's second Game Boy Mega Man is labeled Mega Man II(3Ds/GB). The 1991 cartridge continues the handheld remix line rather than porting one NES number straight across.
tintin-in-tibet: Infogrames' Tintin in Tibet is a 1995 platformer based on the Herge album. Super Nintendo, Game Boy, and other versions retell that mountain rescue.
street-racer: Vivid Image's Street Racer is a 1994 cartoon kart racer on Super Nintendo and Genesis, built to sit beside Mario Kart. Ubisoft published it.
mtvs-beavis-and-butt-head: The MTV cartoon licensed MTV's Beavis and Butt-Head in 1994, one of several console and handheld versions sold that year. Couch gags and the duo's faces are the hook.
donkey-kong-land-2: Rare's Donkey Kong Land 2 is the 1996 Game Boy companion to Donkey Kong Country 2, with Diddy and Dixie on a new handheld map. It is not a compressed port of the Super Nintendo game.
mr-nutz: Ocean's squirrel platformer Mr. Nutz started on Amiga and Super Nintendo around 1994. A Game Boy version carried the same acorn-hoarding hero.
the-final-fantasy-legend: Square's first SaGa game reached the West as The Final Fantasy Legend, a 1989 Game Boy cartridge. Japan called it Makai Toushi SaGa, and the Final Fantasy label was a Western branding.
who-framed-roger-rabbit: The 1988 Touchstone film that mixes cartoons with live action licensed Who Framed Roger Rabbit. Home versions, including a Game Boy game from Capcom in some regions, adapt that case.
kid-dracula: Konami's comic parody of Castlevania reached Game Boy in the West as Kid Dracula in 1993. The Famicom original, Akumajo Special: Boku Dracula-kun, came first.
asterix: The Goscinny and Uderzo comics licensed Asterix (1993), one of Infogrames' many Gaulish platformers. The year baked into the name marks that particular release.
mega-man-iii: Capcom's third Game Boy Mega Man, Mega Man III, arrived in 1992 and folds in bosses associated with the NES Mega Man 3 and 4. It remains a handheld remix.
pokemon-puzzle-challenge: Intelligent Systems recast Panel de Pon with pocket monsters for Pokémon Puzzle Challenge, a 2000 Game Boy Color stack-matcher. Japan sold it as Pokemon de Panepon.
fifa-road-to-world-cup-98: EA Sports' FIFA: Road to World Cup 98 is the 1997 soccer annual aimed at the upcoming World Cup. Nintendo 64 and Game Boy were among the many versions.
bomb-jack: Tehkan's 1984 arcade platformer Bomb Jack scores you for collecting bombs in the right order before they go off. Home computers of the era picked it up quickly.
kirbys-pinball-land-1993: HAL Laboratory's Game Boy pinball table starring the pink hero is Kirby's Pinball Land (1993). Three themed boards and a boss fight up top define that handheld original.
tecmo-bowl-1990: Tecmo's football game Tecmo Bowl (1990) is famous on the NES for calling plays from a set playbook. That coaching choice, more than any one console, is the public memory.
boxing-1980: Bob Whitehead designed Activision's Atari 2600 cartridge Boxing (1980), a two-player bout from the company's early sports line.
final-fantasy-legend-iii: Square's third SaGa, out in Japan in 1991, is Final Fantasy Legend III in the West. Time travel frames this Game Boy party, still sold under the Final Fantasy label abroad.
stargate-1995: The Roland Emmerich film about an ancient portal licensed Stargate (1995). Acclaim's home versions sit with that movie year already printed in the name.
pocket-monsters-pokemon-green-version: Game Freak's Japanese retail pair was Red and Pocket Monsters (Pokemon Green Version), both in 1996. The later Japanese Blue, not this green cart, supplied more of what international Red and Blue became.
kick-off: Dino Dini's Kick Off is the 1989 Anco soccer game whose speed on Amiga and Atari ST made it a rival to later Sensible Soccer. A Game Boy version exists.
metal-gear-solid-1: Hideo Kojima's 1998 PlayStation game Metal Gear Solid is the first 3D Metal Gear. A later Game Boy Color cartridge used this same title in the West for a different story, Ghost Babel.
grand-theft-auto-2-1999: DMA Design's Grand Theft Auto 2 stays top-down in 1999 and adds gang respect meters. The Game Boy Color cartridge is a smaller, separate city.
alone-in-the-dark-the-new-nightmare: Infogrames revived Edward Carnby in Alone in the Dark: The New Nightmare, a 2001 survival-horror sequel. The Game Boy Color edition is its own 2D game, apart from the console release.
driver: Reflections' undercover-driver game Driver (1999) made film-style car chases a PlayStation hit. A later Game Boy Color version is a much smaller take on the same premise.
heroes-of-might-and-magic: New World Computing's first Heroes game, Heroes of Might and Magic: A Strategic Quest, is the 1995 turn-based strategy of heroes, towns, and creature stacks. A Game Boy Color version arrived years later.
rayman: Michel Ancel's limbless hero debuted in Ubisoft's Rayman in 1995, first shown on the Atari Jaguar. Later Game Boy Color and DS cartridges reuse the name with their own stages.
catwoman: Electronic Arts' Catwoman is the 2004 tie-in to the Halle Berry film. GameCube carries a 3D version, and Game Boy Advance has a separate side-scroller.
fifa-2000: EA Sports shipped FIFA 2000 in 1999, naming the soccer annual for the season ahead. A Game Boy Color edition sat beside the console and PC copies.
gex-enter-the-gecko: Crystal Dynamics' TV-quoting gecko returns in Gex: Enter the Gecko (1998), a 3D platformer on PlayStation and Nintendo 64. The Game Boy Color cartridge is a separate 2D version.
donald-duck-goin-quackers: Ubisoft's 2000 Disney platformer Donald Duck: Goin' Quackers is called Quack Attack in Europe. Nintendo 64, GameCube, and Game Boy Color each received a version.
vigilante-8: Luxoflux's Vigilante 8 is a 1998 car-combat game set in an alternate 1970s, on PlayStation and Nintendo 64. A Game Boy Color adaptation followed.
lego-racers: High Voltage Software built LEGO Racers in 1999 for LEGO Media, a kart racer with brick-built cars. Nintendo 64 got that game, and Game Boy Color got a smaller circuit set.
road-rash-ii: Electronic Arts' Genesis sequel Road Rash II adds split-screen to the motorcycle combat of Road Rash. Punching rivals while racing is still the point.
jet-set-radio-2012: Smilebit's Jet Set Radio is the 2000 Dreamcast game about inline crews tagging a city, drawn in cel shading to a pirate-radio beat.
doom-ii: id Software's DOOM II is the 1994 sequel subtitled Hell on Earth, moving the fights into city levels. A Game Boy Advance port years later cut the episode down to fit.
need-for-speed-underground-2-2: EA Black Box's Need for Speed: Underground 2 is the 2004 street-racing sequel with an open city and deep car customization. GameCube has that structure; the Game Boy Advance cart is a separate racer.
splinter-cell: Ubisoft introduced Sam Fisher in Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell, a 2002 stealth game that started on Xbox. GameCube received it, and the Game Boy Advance edition is a separate 2D mission set.
need-for-speed-carbon: EA's Need For Speed Carbon follows Most Wanted in 2006 with canyon duels and a racing crew. GameCube, Wii, and Nintendo DS versions were sold, the handheld ones built as their own games.
sonic-the-hedgehog: Sega's Genesis mascot debuts in Sonic the Hedgehog (1991), built by Sonic Team as a speedy answer to Mario. Later Wii and 3DS reissues are that 16-bit game, not a new adventure.
worms-blast: Team17 left the usual turn-based battles for Worms Blast, a 2002 puzzle closer to block-clearing. GameCube and Game Boy Advance both got versions.
marvel-ult-alliance: Raven Software's Marvel Ultimate Alliance is Activision's 2006 team brawler, switching among Marvel heroes. Wii has that console game, and Game Boy Advance has a smaller separate one.
the-sims-2: Maxis's The Sims 2 is the 2004 PC sequel that adds life stages and aspirations. GameCube and Game Boy Advance releases are separate console games, not the computer simulation shrunk down.
phoenix-wright-ace-attorney-2001: Capcom's courtroom adventure Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney first shipped on the Game Boy Advance in Japan in 2001. The Nintendo DS version that traveled worldwide adds a bonus case and touch-screen evidence.
comix-zone-1995: Sega's 1995 Genesis brawler Comix Zone fights through the panels of a living comic. A Wii Virtual Console release later reissued that same cartridge.
rayman-raving-rabbids: Ubisoft's Rayman Raving Rabbids became a 2006 Wii party disc of motion minigames after starting life as a platformer. Game Boy Advance and Nintendo DS copies are separate products.
oddworld-munchs-oddysee-2001: Oddworld Inhabitants followed Abe with Oddworld: Munch's Oddysee (2001), an Xbox game that pairs him with a new Gabbit ally. A later Game Boy Advance version retells that journey in 2D.
spider-man-2: Treyarch's open-city web-swinging tie-in to Sam Raimi's second film is sold here as Spider-Man 2: The Game. The 2004 GameCube version is that sandbox; Game Boy Advance is a side-scroller.
king-kong: Ubisoft's Peter Jackson's King Kong: The Official Game of the Movie is the 2005 tie-in that alternates a first-person explorer with Kong himself. GameCube has the main design; Game Boy Advance and DS editions are separate.
splinter-cell-pandora-tomorrow: Ubisoft's 2004 sequel Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Pandora Tomorrow is the first Splinter Cell with spies-versus-mercenaries multiplayer. GameCube has that game, and Game Boy Advance has a 2D side story.
harry-potter-and-the-order-of-the-phoeni: Electronic Arts' Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix is the 2007 tie-in to the fifth book and film, built around casting spells in Hogwarts. Wii, DS, and Game Boy Advance each got a version fitted to that hardware.
ultimate-spider-man: Treyarch's Ultimate Spider-Man is a 2005 open-city game based on the Ultimate comics, and you can switch to Venom. GameCube has the 3D version; the handheld editions are separate.
need-for-speed-porsche-unleashed: EA's Need for Speed: Porsche Unleashed traces a career through Porsche history and was sold in Europe as Porsche 2000. The Game Boy Advance cartridge keeps the badge and strips the structure down.
tron-20: Monolith's Tron 2.0 is a 2003 PC sequel set inside the Tron computer world, with disc combat and light cycles. The Game Boy Advance release is a separate action game on that license.
lego-star-wars: Traveller's Tales' first brick Star Wars, Lego Star Wars: The Video Game, retells the prequel trilogy in 2005. GameCube supports co-op play, and Game Boy Advance has a simpler tie-in.
the-lord-of-the-rings-he-return-of-the-k: EA's The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King is a 2003 hack-and-slash of the third Jackson film, with two-player co-op on GameCube. The Game Boy Advance version covers the same war from the side.
shrek-2: Activision's Shrek 2: The Game is the 2004 tie-in to the DreamWorks sequel. GameCube and Game Boy Advance received different versions of that license.
phoenix-wright-ace-attorney-trials-and-t: The third Ace Attorney casebook, Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney − Trials and Tribulations, debuted on the Game Boy Advance in Japan in 2004. DS, Wii, and 3DS releases later carried those trials onward.
phoenix-wright-ace-attorney-justice-for-: Capcom's second Ace Attorney game, Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney − Justice for All, arrived on the Game Boy Advance in Japan in 2002. The Western DS release came later, with the same four cases.
madagascar: Activision's Madagascar is a 2005 tie-in to the DreamWorks zoo-animal film. GameCube, Game Boy Advance, and Nintendo DS each shipped their own version.
lego-star-wars-2-the-original-trilogy: Traveller's Tales followed the prequel game with Lego Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy in 2006, a brick retelling of the first three films. GameCube has co-op, and Game Boy Advance has its own version.
final-fantasy-ii: Square's 1988 Famicom sequel FINAL FANTASY II raises stats by using weapons and spells, with no experience points. Game Boy Advance and Wii releases later reissued that game.
tony-hawks-underground-2: Neversoft's Tony Hawk's Underground 2 is the 2004 skate sequel that leans into a stunt-tour story. GameCube has that campaign; the Game Boy Advance cart is a separate adaptation.
tony-hawks-pro-skater-4: Neversoft's Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 4 is the 2002 entry that drops the two-minute run timer for open goals. GameCube uses that structure, and Game Boy Advance has a different skate game under the name.
fifa-07: EA Sports' FIFA 07 covers the 2006 season and was a launch game on PlayStation 3 as well as on the older consoles.
crash-of-the-titans: Radical Entertainment's Crash of the Titans is a 2007 Crash game about grabbing oversized enemies and turning them. Wii, DS, and Game Boy Advance versions differ from one another.
broken-sword-the-shadow-of-the-templars: Revolution Software's Broken Sword 1 - The Shadow of the Templars is the 1996 point-and-click about an American tourist pulled into a Templar plot in Paris. A Game Boy Advance port arrived later.
ratatouille: THQ's Ratatouille is the 2007 tie-in to Pixar's film about a rat in a Paris kitchen. GameCube, Game Boy Advance, and DS were sold as separate games.
avatar-tla-tbe: THQ's second Avatar tie-in, Avatar: The Last Airbender - The Burning Earth, covers the show's Earth Kingdom war in 2007. Game Boy Advance and Nintendo DS each have a version.
wizardry-proving-grounds-of-the-mad-over: Sir-Tech's Wizardry: Proving Grounds of the Mad Overlord is the 1981 Apple II dungeon crawl, by Andrew Greenberg and Robert Woodhead, that set the party-based first-person template. Japanese Game Boy Color releases later carried the early scenarios.
nhl-2000: EA Sports' hockey annual NHL 2000 shipped in 1999 under the following year's name. A Game Boy Color edition was made for that season.
moorhuhn-3: Germany's Crazy Chicken fad continued with Moorhuhn 3, a 2001 entry in the deliberately silly hunting series. A Game Boy Color version put that joke on a cartridge.
perfect-dark-2000: Rare's Perfect Dark (GBC) is a 2000 Game Boy Color mission set starring Joanna Dark, built as a stealth-leaning companion to the Nintendo 64 shooter. It is not that console campaign cut down.
rainbow-islands-the-story-of-bubble-bobb: Taito's arcade follow-up to Bubble Bobble is Rainbow Islands: The Story of Bubble Bobble 2, swapping bubbles for rainbows you climb. The 1987 cabinet was ported to many home systems afterward.
frogger-2-swampys-revenge: Hasbro's Frogger 2: Swampy's Revenge is a 2000 sequel to the Frogger revival, with more obstacle courses and a named villain in the title. Game Boy Color was one of the versions.
mega-man-xtreme-2000: Capcom's Game Boy Color X entry Mega Man Xtreme remixes stages from the first two Mega Man X games. North America received that cartridge in 2001.
test-drive-off-road-3: Accolade's dirt-racing line continued with Test Drive: Off-Road 3 in 1999. A Game Boy Color edition was issued under the same off-road name.
resident-evil-gaiden: Capcom's Resident Evil Gaiden is a 2001 Game Boy Color side story set on a cruise ship, developed outside the main survival-horror team. It does not port any console Resident Evil.
wwf-attitude: Acclaim's WWF Attitude is the 1999 wrestling game covering the Attitude Era roster, on Nintendo 64 and PlayStation. Game Boy Color has a reduced take on that license.
mega-man-xtreme-2-2001: Capcom's Mega Man Xtreme 2 is the 2001 Game Boy Color follow-up, with a parts system and bosses drawn from Mega Man X3. It stayed a handheld-only X game.
army-men-sarges-heroes-2: 3DO's Army Men: Sarge's Heroes 2 is the 2000 sequel about green plastic soldiers at war with the tan army. Nintendo 64 has the 3D game, and Game Boy Color has a separate version.
wizardry-ii-the-knight-of-diamonds: Sir-Tech's Wizardry II: The Knight of Diamonds is the 1982 sequel, a shorter scenario that imports a party from the first dungeon. It belongs to the original Apple II Wizardry line.
kirby-tilt-n-tumble: HAL and Nintendo's Kirby Tilt 'n' Tumble reads a tilt sensor inside the 2000 Game Boy Color cartridge, so you tip the whole handheld to roll Kirby. The gimmick is the game.
looney-tunes-racing: Infogrames' Looney Tunes Racing is a 2000 kart racer starring the Warner cartoon cast. A Game Boy Color version sits beside the PlayStation release.
toki-tori-2001: Two Tribes' egg-collecting puzzle Toki Tori (2001) is a Game Boy Color original about a small chick. Later Wii and 3DS releases remake this handheld game.
rampage-2-universal-tour: Midway's Rampage 2: Universal Tour sends George, Lizzie, and Ralph off Earth in 1999 to smash cities on other worlds.
disneys-dinosaur: Disney's prehistoric film licensed Disney's Dinosaur in 2000. The Game Boy Color cartridge is one of several home versions sold with that movie.
test-drive-le-mans: Infogrames' Test Drive Le Mans, also sold as Le Mans 24 Hours, is a 2000 endurance racer built around the French day-long race. A Game Boy Color version carries the same event.
hugo-black-diamond-fever: The Danish TV troll returns in Hugo: Black Diamond Fever, a 2001 entry from Interactive Television Entertainment's long Hugo line. Game Boy Color is one of many Hugo cartridges.
daikatana-2: John Romero's Ion Storm shooter Daikatana is the 2000 PC game whose long delay became infamous. The Game Boy Color release is a separate action game, not that first-person project.
yars-revenge-2: Howard Scott Warshaw's Yars' Revenge is the 1982 Atari 2600 cartridge that became one of the console's biggest original sellers. The insect-versus-shield battle is an Atari design.
the-lion-king-simbas-mighty-adventure: Activision's The Lion King: Simba's Mighty Adventure is a 2000 follow-up to the earlier Lion King platformer, covering scenes past the first film. PlayStation and Game Boy Color both had versions.
wizardry-iii-legacy-of-llylgamyn: Sir-Tech's third scenario, Wizardry III: Legacy of Llylgamyn, arrived in 1983 and shifts the dungeon crawl toward a new generation of heroes. It closes the original Apple II trilogy.
pokemon-puzzle-challenge-2000: Intelligent Systems recast Panel de Pon with Pokémon faces for Pokémon Puzzle Challenge (2000). Clearing stacks is the whole contest, and it is the color-handheld cousin of Pokémon Puzzle League rather than a Red or Blue adventure.
harvest-moon-gb: The first handheld Harvest Moon is Harvest Moon GB, a 1997 farm sim from Victor Interactive, published in the West by Natsume. Crops, livestock, and town visits fill the cartridge.
f1-racing-championship: Ubisoft's official Formula 1 license F1 Racing Championship reached Nintendo 64 in 2000. The Game Boy Color edition is a simpler racer under the same name.
dragon-ball-z-legendary-super-warriors: Banpresto's Dragon Ball Z: Legendary Super Warriors is a 2002 Game Boy Color strategy game that retells major Dragon Ball Z fights with a card-like battle system. Infogrames published it in the West.
azure-dreams: Konami's tower-climbing monster game reached Game Boy Color as Azure Dreams GB in 1999, a handheld companion to the PlayStation release. Random floors and egg hatching remain the loop.
donkey-kong-land-iii: Rare's Donkey Kong Land 3 is the 1997 handheld companion to Donkey Kong Country 3, starring Dixie and Kiddy. Color hardware shows off what the Game Boy version started.
kirikou: Michel Ocelot's French animated film licensed Kirikou, a 2001 Game Boy Color release aimed at European players. It is a cartoon adaptation, not a Nintendo adventure.
mickeys-speedway-usa: Rare's Mickey's Speedway USA is a 2000 kart racer starring Mickey and the Disney cast, made for Nintendo 64. The Game Boy Color version is a separate top-down circuit game.
nascar-heat: Hasbro's NASCAR Heat is a 2000 stock-car license for that NASCAR season. PlayStation, PC, and Game Boy Color all carried editions.
harvest-moon-2-gbc-1999: Harvest Moon 2 GBC (1999) is Natsume's sequel to Harvest Moon GB, with a bigger town and more villagers than that first cartridge. It sits between the original Game Boy farm and Harvest Moon 3 GBC.
harry-potter-quidditch-world-cup: EA's Harry Potter: Quidditch World Cup is a 2003 sports game about the broomstick matches from the books. GameCube has the 3D version, and Game Boy Advance has a simpler adaptation.
tony-hawks-underground: Neversoft's Tony Hawk's Underground is the 2003 skate game that adds a story and lets you get off the board. GameCube has that campaign; Game Boy Advance is a separate skate title.
james-bond-007-nightfire: Eurocom's James Bond 007: NightFire is EA's 2002 Bond shooter, a follow-up to Agent Under Fire. GameCube has the main missions, and Game Boy Advance is a separate first-person take.
kingdom-hearts-chain-of-memories: Square Enix and Jupiter's Kingdom Hearts: Chain of Memories is the 2004 Game Boy Advance entry set between the first two Kingdom Hearts games. Fights run on a deck of cards, and a later PlayStation 2 remix rebuilds it in 3D.
toy-story-2-buzz-lightyear-to-the-rescue: Traveller's Tales' Toy Story 2: Buzz Lightyear to the Rescue is Activision's 1999 3D platformer based on the Pixar sequel. Nintendo 64 received that console game.
baldurs-gate-dark-alliance: Snowblind Studios' Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance is a 2001 console hack-and-slash in the Forgotten Realms, separate from BioWare's PC Baldur's Gate. GameCube got a port, and a Game Boy Advance game later used the name.
teenage-mutant-ninja-turtles-2003: Konami's beat-em-up based on the cartoon that premiered the same year is Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (2003). GameCube has the 3D brawler, and Game Boy Advance has a side-scrolling counterpart.
pokemon-mystery-dungeon-blue-rescue-team: On Nintendo DS, Chunsoft's Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Blue Rescue Team is where a human wakes as a Pokemon and takes rescue jobs in 2005. The cartridge can link jobs with its Game Boy Advance partner.
medal-of-honor-underground: DreamWorks Interactive's Medal of Honor: Underground is a 2000 PlayStation follow-up that follows French fighter Manon through World War II. The Game Boy Advance release is a later, separate shooter.
colin-mcrae-rally-20: Codemasters' Colin McRae Rally 2.0 is the 2000 rally sequel named for the Scottish champion, built around stage times. A Game Boy Advance version followed as a handheld adaptation.
the-lord-of-the-rings-the-two-towers: EA's The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers is the 2002 action game of the second Jackson film, including Helm's Deep. GameCube has the 3D battles, and Game Boy Advance has its own side-view campaign.
worms-world-party: Team17's Worms World Party is a 2001 party-minded entry in the artillery series. The Game Boy Advance version keeps those turn-based worm battles on a small screen.
madden-nfl-07: EA Sports' Madden NFL 07 is the football annual for the 2006 season, and it launched on PlayStation 3 alongside the older consoles.
ford-racing-3: The licensed Ford lineup racer Ford Racing 3 arrived in 2005. Game Boy Advance and Nintendo DS versions are the handheld editions of that license.
pirates-of-the-caribbean: Disney's pirate license reached Game Boy Advance as Pirates of the Caribbean in 2003, the year the first film opened. The cartridge is a handheld adventure under that name.
castlevania-harmony-of-dissonance-2: Konami's Castlevania: Harmony of Dissonance is the 2002 Game Boy Advance follow-up to Circle of the Moon, with Juste Belmont exploring a twin castle. It is a brighter, larger handheld original.
the-incredibles: THQ's The Incredibles is the 2004 tie-in to Pixar's superhero film. GameCube has the console adventure, and Game Boy Advance has a separate side-scroller.
2006-fifa-world-cup: EA Sports' official tournament game 2006 FIFA World Cup covers the national teams in Germany. GameCube and Game Boy Advance each received an edition.
the-legend-of-zelda-four-swords: Nintendo and Capcom's The Legend of Zelda: Four Swords is the 2002 multiplayer quest first packed with the Game Boy Advance port of A Link to the Past. Later DS and 3DS releases revisited four Links at once.
open-season: Ubisoft's Open Season is the 2006 tie-in to the Sony hunting-season cartoon. Game Boy Advance, GameCube, and Nintendo DS were sold as separate games.
castlevania-circle-of-the-moon-2: Konami launched the Game Boy Advance with Castlevania: Circle of the Moon in 2001, using paired cards for magic. In Japan it was sold as Akumajo Dracula: Circle of the Moon, outside the usual numbering.
bionicle-heroes: Eidos published Bionicle Heroes in 2006, an action game based on LEGO's Bionicle toys. GameCube, Game Boy Advance, and DS versions each use that license differently.
madden-nfl-06: EA Sports' Madden NFL 06, released in 2005, adds a quarterback vision cone that hides receivers outside the passer's view.
the-lord-of-the-rings-the-fellowship-of-: Vivendi's The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring is a 2002 tie-in to the first Jackson film, a different product from EA's later movie brawlers. The Game Boy Advance version follows that journey in handheld form.
heart-of-darkness: Amazing Studio's Heart of Darkness is a 1998 cinematic platformer published by Interplay on PC and PlayStation, after a long development. Set-piece scenes are what the game is remembered for.
sonic-advance: Dimps and Sonic Team's Sonic Advance is the 2001 Game Boy Advance platformer, the first Sonic built for that handheld. You can switch among a small cast at high speed.
spongebob-squarepants-battle-for-bikini-: Heavy Iron's SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom is THQ's 2003 platformer, later remade as Rehydrated. GameCube has the 3D adventure, and Game Boy Advance is a separate side-scroller.
mortal-kombat-deadly-alliance: Midway's Mortal Kombat: Deadly Alliance is the 2002 fighter that moved the series into 3D and gave each kombatant two fatality styles. GameCube has that game; Game Boy Advance has a smaller 2D reading.
star-wars-episode-iii-revenge-of-the-sit: LucasArts' Star Wars: Episode III: Revenge of the Sith is the 2005 tie-in to the third prequel film. Game Boy Advance and Nintendo DS retell the movie as handheld action games.
the-spongebob-squarepants-movie: THQ's The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie is the 2004 tie-in to the first SpongeBob feature. GameCube has a 3D version, and Game Boy Advance has a side-scrolling one.
street-fighter-alpha-3-1998: Capcom closed the Alpha line with Street Fighter Alpha 3 (1998), an arcade fighter known for a huge roster and the ISM style selects. The Game Boy Advance port is a celebrated conversion that adds still more fighters.
crash-nitro-kart: Vicarious Visions' Crash Nitro Kart is the 2003 kart follow-up to Crash Team Racing. GameCube and Game Boy Advance both have versions, the handheld one built separately.
over-the-hedge: Activision's Over the Hedge is the 2006 tie-in to the DreamWorks film about suburban animals. GameCube, Game Boy Advance, and DS each got a version.
ssx-tricky: EA Sports BIG's SSX Tricky is the 2001 snowboard sequel that exaggerates the trick system of the first SSX. GameCube has the main game, and Game Boy Advance has a reduced adaptation.
fifa-2005: EA Canada shipped FIFA 2005 in 2004 with a first-touch system that changes how a trap sets up the next pass.
pong-1972: Al Alcorn's paddle tennis for Atari is Pong (1972), the arcade rally that became a commercial phenomenon. Decades of reissues followed that cabinet.
fifa-06: EA Sports' FIFA 06 covers the 2005 season and was ready for the Xbox 360 launch as well as for older consoles.
cave-story-doukutsu-monogatari: Daisuke Amaya, working as Pixel, gave away Cave Story: Doukutsu Monogatari for PC in 2004. Later paid ports, including a Nintendo 3DS eShop release, spread that one-person platformer.
meet-the-robinsons: Disney's Meet the Robinsons is the 2007 tie-in to the time-travel cartoon. Game Boy Advance and GameCube versions shipped with the film.
sonic-advance-3: Dimps' Sonic Advance 3 is the 2004 Game Boy Advance platformer that pairs Sonic with a partner who changes his moves. It is the third Advance game and stayed on that handheld.
pokemon-mystery-dungeon-red-rescue-team: Nintendo's Game Boy Advance rescue story Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Red Rescue Team shares a 2005 plot with a DS partner cart, both made by Chunsoft. Friend rescue codes pass between those two editions.
fifa-2004: EA Sports released FIFA 2004 in 2003 and switched offsides off after complaints about the previous annual.
super-mario-advance: Nintendo's Super Mario Advance is the 2001 Game Boy Advance remake of Super Mario Bros. 2, the game that began as Doki Doki Panic. A two-player Mario Bros. mode is included.
x2-wolverines-revenge: Activision's X2: Wolverine's Revenge is a 2003 Wolverine action game sold around the X2 film. GameCube and Game Boy Advance received different versions.
teenage-mutant-ninja-turtles-2-battle-ne: Konami's Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles 2: Battle Nexus is the 2004 cartoon follow-up named for a multiverse tournament. You clear ladders of fighters between story stages.
sonic-advance-2: Dimps' Sonic Advance 2 is the 2002 Game Boy Advance sequel built around a boost that sends Sonic uphill. Cream the Rabbit joins the playable cast here.
dead-to-rights: Namco's Dead to Rights is a 2002 third-person shooter about a cop whose dog fights beside him. GameCube ports the console game, and Game Boy Advance is a separate side-scroller.
cars: THQ's Cars is the 2006 racing game based on the Pixar film. GameCube has the console racer, and Game Boy Advance has a smaller licensed version.
the-chronicles-of-narnia-the-lion-the-wi: Disney's The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, The Witch, and The Wardrobe is the 2005 action game based on the Walden film. GameCube and Game Boy Advance each retell that story for their hardware.
surfs-up: Ubisoft's Surf's Up is the 2007 tie-in to the penguin-surfing film. Game Boy Advance and GameCube versions shipped with the movie.
super-mario-world-super-mario-advance-2: Nintendo's Super Mario World: Super Mario Advance 2 is the 2001 Game Boy Advance port of Super Mario World. Luigi is playable from the start, which the Super Nintendo original did not allow.
bionicle-the-game: LEGO's Bionicle storyline licensed Bionicle: The Game in 2003. GameCube and Game Boy Advance each received an action version of those toy heroes.
turok-evolution: Acclaim's Turok: Evolution is the 2002 prequel in the dinosaur-hunting series. GameCube has the first-person game, and Game Boy Advance has a separate side-scroller.
tom-clancys-rainbow-six-rogue-spear: Red Storm's Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six: Rogue Spear is the 1999 tactical shooter that followed Rainbow Six. The Game Boy Advance cartridge is a later handheld mission set, not the PC planner.
top-spin-2: 2K Sports' tennis sequel Top Spin 2 arrived in 2006 with an emphasis on shot timing. The Game Boy Advance release is the handheld edition of that license.
x-men-the-official-game: Activision's X-Men: The Official Game fills the gap between the X2 and X3 films in 2006, with Wolverine, Iceman, and Nightcrawler among the leads.
shark-tale: Activision's Shark Tale is the 2004 tie-in to the DreamWorks underwater film. GameCube and Game Boy Advance each have a version.
the-urbz-sims-in-the-city: EA's The Urbz: Sims in the City is a 2004 console spinoff that follows street crews instead of suburban lots. GameCube and Game Boy Advance versions were built for those machines.
fantastic-four: Activision's Fantastic Four is the 2005 tie-in to the Marvel film. GameCube and Game Boy Advance let you use the four heroes in separate adaptations.
batman-begins: Eurocom's Batman Begins is EA's 2005 stealth action tie-in to Nolan's film. GameCube has that design, and Game Boy Advance has a separate version.
batman-vengeance: Ubisoft's Batman: Vengeance draws on The New Batman Adventures in 2001, pitting Batman against that cartoon's villains rather than a movie plot.
the-simpsons-road-rage: Radical Entertainment's The Simpsons: Road Rage sends Springfield locals on fare-chasing drives in 2001, published by Electronic Arts. Homer, Bart, and other regulars each get a car.
yoshis-island-super-mario-advance-3: Nintendo's Yoshi's Island: Super Mario Advance 3 is the 2002 Game Boy Advance port of Super Mario World 2: Yoshi's Island. Extra stages sit beyond the Super Nintendo set.
the-incredibles-the-mr-drill-attack: THQ's The Incredibles: Rise of the Underminer picks up after the Pixar film in 2005 and makes the Underminer the threat. Mr. Incredible shares the dig with Frozone.
killswitch: Namco's Kill Switch is a 2003 third-person shooter often credited with popularizing a dedicated cover button. The Game Boy Advance version is a handheld take on that idea.
asterix-obelix-xxl: The Goscinny and Uderzo comics supply Asterix & Obelix XXL - Kick Buttix!, a 2004 handheld entry in the Asterix and Obelix XXL line. Game Boy Advance uses the Kick Buttix name on the box.
shining-force-1992: Sega's first strategy RPG in the line, Shining Force: The Legacy of Great Intention, arrived on the Genesis in 1992, developed with Climax. A later Game Boy Advance remake reworks that campaign.
shrek-superslam: Activision's Shrek SuperSlam is a 2005 arena fighter starring the DreamWorks cast. The Game Boy Advance version is a handheld brawler under that name.
mario-vs-donkey-kong: Nintendo Software Technology's puzzle chase Mario vs. Donkey Kong (2004) succeeds the 1994 Game Boy Donkey Kong. Mario pursues toy Mini-Marios through construction-site stages.
finding-nemo: THQ's Finding Nemo is the 2003 tie-in to the Pixar ocean film. The Game Boy Advance version is a side-scrolling adaptation of that movie.
pac-man-world-2: Namco's 3D platformer sequel Pac-Man World 2 (2002) sends Pac-Man after ghosts who stole the golden fruit. A Game Boy Advance version turns that quest into a handheld platformer.
robots: The Blue Sky robot-city film licensed Robots in 2005. The Game Boy Advance version is the handheld edition of that movie tie-in.
pink-panther-pinkadelic-pursuit: The cartoon panther licensed Pink Panther: Pinkadelic Pursuit in 2003, a platformer sold in Europe and North America. Game Boy Advance is one of the versions.
star-wars-episode-i-jedi-power-battles: LucasArts' Star Wars Episode I: Jedi Power Battles is a 2000 brawler through the first prequel, with two players as Jedi. It launched on PlayStation, and a Dreamcast version followed.
mega-man-zero-2002: Inti Creates' Mega Man Zero starts a new Capcom series on the Game Boy Advance in 2002, set after the X games. High difficulty and cyber-elves define that handheld original.
avatar-the-last-airbender: THQ's Avatar: The Last Airbender is the 2006 action game based on the Nickelodeon series. The Game Boy Advance version is a side-scrolling tie-in to the bending battles.
grand-theft-auto-advance: Digital Eclipse developed Grand Theft Auto Advance for Rockstar in 2004, a top-down Game Boy Advance story of its own. It does not port Grand Theft Auto III.
harvest-moon-friends-of-mineral-town-200: Marvelous remade Back to Nature on the Game Boy Advance as Harvest Moon: Friends of Mineral Town. Natsume published that 2003 Western farm sim.
alien-hominid: The Behemoth's run-and-gun Alien Hominid began as a Newgrounds Flash cartoon and reached consoles in 2004. The hand-drawn look stayed intact on the retail versions.
the-legend-of-spyro-a-new-beginning: Krome Studios' The Legend of Spyro: A New Beginning is Vivendi's 2006 reboot, a darker origin for Spyro. The Game Boy Advance version is a separate 2D adaptation of that restart.
mega-man-battle-network-2001: Capcom's Mega Man Battle Network starts a 2001 Game Boy Advance RPG about net battles fought with collectible chips. It stands apart from the classic platformers.
hitman-2-silent-assassin: IO Interactive's Hitman 2: Silent Assassin is the 2002 stealth sequel that set Agent 47's contract structure. A GameCube port brought those missions to Nintendo's console.
tomb-raider-legend: Crystal Dynamics rebooted Lara Croft with Tomb Raider: Legend in 2006, that studio's first Tomb Raider. GameCube received a port of the console adventure.
star-wars-jedi-knight-ii-jedi-outcast: Raven Software's Star Wars Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast returns Kyle Katarn to a lightsaber in 2002. LucasArts published it, including a GameCube version.
prince-of-persia-the-sands-of-time: Ubisoft Montreal revived Jordan Mechner's series with Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time in 2003, built around a dagger that rewinds a few seconds of mistakes.
need-for-speed-most-wanted: EA Black Box's Need For Speed: Most Wanted is the 2005 street racer about climbing a blacklist of police and rivals in an open city. The GameCube version is that same pursuit.
prince-of-persia-warrior-within: Ubisoft's Prince of Persia: Warrior Within is the 2004 sequel, a darker follow-up to The Sands of Time with a heavier combat focus. GameCube received that console version.
prince-of-persia-the-two-thrones: Ubisoft closed the Sands trilogy with Prince of Persia: The Two Thrones in 2005, mixing acrobatics with speed kills. GameCube has the original release, and a Wii version followed.
crazy-taxi: Sega's Hitmaker cabinet Crazy Taxi (1999) is a clock-racing fare game that became a Dreamcast hit. The GameCube release is a home port of that arcade design.
sonic-adventure-2: Sonic Team's Sonic Adventure 2 splits into hero and dark stories on the Dreamcast in 2001, and it introduces Shadow. The GameCube Battle edition later added more multiplayer.
sonic-adventure-dx: The 2003 GameCube edition of the Dreamcast original is Sonic Adventure DX: Director's Cut, adding Game Gear games and mission cards. It is an enhanced port, not a new numbered sequel.
kao-the-kangaroo-round-2: Poland's Tate Interactive continued its boxing kangaroo with KAO the Kangaroo: Round 2, a cartoon platformer that reached GameCube. It is the sequel in that European series.
beyond-good-evil: Michel Ancel's Beyond Good & Evil is Ubisoft's 2003 adventure about the photographer Jade on Hillys. The GameCube version is one of the original releases.
splinter-cell-chaos-theory: Ubisoft's third Splinter Cell, Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell Chaos Theory, is the 2005 entry many players treat as the peak of the early stealth games. The Nintendo DS release is a different top-down game.
xiii: Ubisoft's cel-shaded shooter XIII adapts the Belgian comic by Van Hamme and Vance in 2003, cutting between panels as you fight.
tcs-sc-double-agent: The 2006 undercover entry Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell Double Agent shipped as two different campaigns. GameCube and Wii carry the last-generation version, separate from the Xbox 360 game.
red-faction-ii: Volition's Red Faction II leaves the first game's destructible Mars tunnels for a more linear 2002 campaign with squad chatter.
street-racing-syndicate: Eutechnyx's Street Racing Syndicate is a 2004 street racer that mixes races with a city nightlife scene. GameCube shipped alongside the PlayStation 2 and Xbox versions.
need-for-speed-underground-3: EA Black Box turned the series toward illegal street racing with Need for Speed: Underground in 2003. The GameCube version is that pink-slip career.
sonic-the-hedgehog-2: Sega's Sonic the Hedgehog 2 is the 1992 Genesis sequel that introduces Tails and the spin dash. Later Wii and 3DS releases reissue that 16-bit game.
resident-evil-2002: Shinji Mikami directed Capcom's GameCube remake Resident Evil (2002), a full rebuild of the 1996 mansion. A Wii edition later reissued that same remake.
broken-sword-3-the-sleeping-dragon: Revolution Software's Broken Sword 3 - The Sleeping Dragon is the 2003 sequel, the first Broken Sword in 3D. George and Nico return, and GameCube was among the platforms.
bloodrayne: Terminal Reality's BloodRayne is Majesco's 2002 action game about a dhampir agent. GameCube is one of the console versions, and a film later used the name.
gun: Neversoft's western GUN is a 2005 revenge story on horseback, published by Activision. The GameCube version is that open-country shooter.
the-sims: Will Wright and Maxis's The Sims is the 2000 PC phenomenon about household needs. The GameCube release is a separate console game inspired by it.
harry-potter-and-the-chamber-of-secrets: EA's Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets is the 2002 tie-in to the second book and film. On GameCube you can roam Hogwarts between classes, a step past the first game.
ikaruga: Treasure's Ikaruga is Hiroshi Iuchi's 2001 shooter, built on swapping black and white polarity to absorb shots. The GameCube disc is a home port of that arcade game.
conflict-desert-storm: Pivotal Games' squad shooter Conflict Desert Storm follows special forces in the Gulf War and was published by SCi. GameCube received a port of that tactical campaign.
killer7: Suda51 and Grasshopper Manufacture's killer7 is Capcom's 2005 on-rails assassin game, drawn in cel shading. It debuted on GameCube and PlayStation 2.
call-of-duty-black-ops: Treyarch's Call of Duty: Black Ops is the 2010 Cold War shooter that opened the Black Ops line. A Wii version shipped, and the Nintendo DS edition is a separate portable campaign.
call-of-duty-modern-warfare-3: Infinity Ward and Sledgehammer closed the original Modern Warfare story with Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 in 2011. The Wii version adapts that campaign for motion controls.
lego-lord-of-the-rings: Traveller's Tales' LEGO The Lord of the Rings retells the three Jackson films in 2012 and lets you wander an open Middle-earth between story beats.
tomb-raider-underworld: Crystal Dynamics' Tomb Raider: Underworld continues the Legend-era Lara in 2008. The Wii version is a reduced adaptation, and the DS game is a separate side story.
call-of-duty-world-at-war: Treyarch's Call of Duty: World at War is the 2008 World War II shooter covering the Pacific and the Eastern Front. Wii has a version, and the DS edition is its own portable game.
world-of-goo: 2D Boy's World of Goo is the 2008 physics puzzle about building structures from living goo balls, a PC and WiiWare hit. Nintendo Switch received a port much later.
modern-warfare: Infinity Ward rebooted Call of Duty in the present day with Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare in 2007. A Wii port came later, and the DS version is a separate campaign.
bully-scholarship-edition: Rockstar's Bully: Scholarship Edition is the 2008 expanded release of the 2006 school satire. The Wii version includes the extra classes from that edition.
tomb-raider-anniversary: Crystal Dynamics rebuilt the 1996 mansion raid as Tomb Raider: Anniversary in 2007, using the Legend engine. A Wii version followed the PlayStation 2 and PC releases.
need-for-speed-hot-pursuit-2: Criterion rebooted the police-chase idea as Need For Speed: Hot Pursuit in 2010, with Autolog social features. A Wii version was built around that console's controllers.
far-cry: Crytek's Far Cry is the 2004 PC shooter on a tropical island that launched the series and showed off the first CryEngine.
star-wars-the-force-unleashed-2: LucasArts' STAR WARS: The Force Unleashed II is the 2010 sequel about Starkiller's clone. Wii and Nintendo DS versions are scaled adaptations, apart from the Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3 game.
rayman-origins: Ubisoft Montpellier returned to side-scrolling with Rayman Origins in 2011, playable with up to four characters. Wii and Nintendo 3DS both received that painted platformer.
lego-star-wars-tcs: Traveller's Tales compiled the prequel game and the original-trilogy game as LEGO Star Wars - The Complete Saga in 2007. Wii and Nintendo DS versions include that combined episode list.
lego-batman: Traveller's Tales' first brick Batman, LEGO Batman, arrived in 2008 and splits the campaign between hero chapters and villain chapters.
lego-batman-2: Traveller's Tales' LEGO Batman 2 DC Super Heroes is the 2012 sequel with spoken dialogue and an open Gotham. It reached Wii, Wii U, DS, and 3DS.
cave-story: Nicalis published Cave Story+, the enhanced edition of Daisuke Amaya's freeware, with redrawn art and extra modes. Wii, DS, and 3DS releases carried that version.
mini-ninjas: IO Interactive, the Hitman studio, made the family adventure Mini Ninjas in 2009. Wii and Nintendo DS both received versions about the young ninja.
lego-harry-potter: Traveller's Tales' LEGO Harry Potter: Years 1-4 retells the first four stories in brick form in 2010. Wii and Nintendo DS versions cover those Hogwarts years.
metal-slug-3: SNK's METAL SLUG 3 is the 2000 run-and-gun widely called a high point of the arcade line. A Wii release later brought that Neo Geo game over.
bittrip-runner: Gaijin Games' BIT.TRIP RUNNER is a 2010 WiiWare rhythm game: CommanderVideo auto-runs, and every jump has to stay on the beat. It is the fourth BIT.TRIP release.
back-to-the-future-the-game: Telltale's episodic sequel to the film trilogy is Back to the Future: The Game, from 2010, with Christopher Lloyd returning as Doc. A Wii version collected those episodes.
broken-sword-1-dc-espanol: Revolution's Broken Sword 1 - Shadow of the Templars (The Director's Cut) is the 2009 remake of the 1996 adventure, adding a chapter playable as Nico. Wii and Nintendo DS use that expanded script.
pirates-3: Firaxis remade Meier's 1987 seafaring game in 2004 as Sid Meier's Pirates!, mixing sailing, sword fights, and dancing. The Wii version is a later port of that remake.
uno: Mattel's shedding card game reaches consoles as UNO, matching colors and numbers the way the tabletop deck does. Wii and Nintendo DS editions let a room play without the physical pack.
fifa-14: EA Sports' soccer annual FIFA 14 shipped in 2013. The Wii and Nintendo 3DS editions are separate from the Ignite-engine game on newer consoles.
swords-and-soldiers-hd: Ronimo Games' side-scrolling strategy of Vikings, Aztecs, and Chinese armies was upgraded as Swords and Soldiers HD. The HD edition sharpens the WiiWare original.
lego-harry-potter-years-5-7: Traveller's Tales' LEGO Harry Potter: Years 5-7 covers the last three stories in 2011, from the Order of the Phoenix through the Battle of Hogwarts.
nfs-undercover: EA's Need For Speed Undercover is a 2008 street racer framed as an undercover-cop story in an open city. Wii and Nintendo DS versions are scaled-down games under that name.
sniper-elite: Rebellion's Sniper Elite is the 2005 World War II shooter known for its bullet-camera kills. The Wii release is a later port of that first game.
lego-star-wars-iii: Traveller's Tales' LEGO Star Wars III - The Clone Wars is the 2011 game based on the animated Clone Wars, adding large ground battles. Wii, DS, and 3DS received versions.
and-yet-it-moves: Broken Rules' And Yet It Moves is a 2009 puzzle where you rotate the whole scene so the character can walk on a new surface. The WiiWare version brought that paper-collage idea to a console.
toribash: Nabi Studios' Toribash is a turn-based fighter: you set each joint, then watch the physics play out. The WiiWare release is a console edition of that PC original.
rec-room: Against Gravity launched Rec Room in 2016 as a social virtual-reality hangout full of user-made rooms and mini-games. Players meet as avatars on PC headsets.
toki-tori: Two Tribes reissued the chick's egg hunt as Toki Tori on WiiWare in 2008, after the Game Boy Color original. Later Wii U and 3DS releases keep that puzzle.
lego-indiana-jones: Traveller's Tales' LEGO Indiana Jones: The Original Adventures retells Raiders, Temple of Doom, and The Last Crusade in brick form. Wii and Nintendo DS versions cover those three films.
rayman-3-hoodlum-havoc: Ubisoft's Rayman 3: Hoodlum Havoc sends Rayman against hoodlums in the Glade of Dreams in 2003, and he can lock onto several targets at once.
resident-evil-3-nemesis: Capcom's Resident Evil 3: Nemesis is the 1999 sequel in which Jill flees Raccoon City while Nemesis hunts her. The GameCube version is a later port of that PlayStation game.
sonic-the-hedgehog-3: Sega's Genesis sequel Sonic the Hedgehog 3 (1994) adds save files and a story built to lock onto Sonic & Knuckles. Wii Virtual Console later reissued that 16-bit cartridge.
tom-clancys-ghost-recon: Red Storm's Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon is the 2001 squad shooter about commanding Ghosts in a near-future war. The GameCube version is a console port of that tactical game.
the-simpsons-hit-run: Radical Entertainment's The Simpsons: Hit & Run is a 2003 open-world driving tour of Springfield, published by Vivendi. GameCube is one of the original releases.
star-wars-bounty-hunter: LucasArts' Star Wars Bounty Hunter casts you as Jango Fett in 2002, taking contracts with a jetpack before Attack of the Clones.
harry-potter-and-the-prisoner-of-azkaban: EA's Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban is the 2004 tie-in to the third book and film. The GameCube version adds that year's spells to another Hogwarts roam.
sonic-knuckles: Sega's Sonic & Knuckles is the 1994 Genesis cartridge famous for a lock-on port that clips Sonic 2 or Sonic 3 on top. Knuckles is playable, and later compilations keep that team-up.
need-for-speed-hot-pursuit-2-2: EA's Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit 2 brought police chases back in 2002. The PlayStation 2 version was built by a different team than the GameCube, Xbox, and PC releases.
mario-kart-double-dash: Nintendo's Mario Kart: Double Dash is the 2003 GameCube entry that seats two riders in each kart so a partner can throw items. It is a home-console Mario Kart.
judge-dredd-dredd-vs-death: Rebellion's Judge Dredd: Dredd vs. Death pits the 2000 AD lawman against the Dark Judges in 2003, and you can book perps between firefights.
freedom-fighters: IO Interactive's Freedom Fighters is a 2003 shooter set in an alternate New York occupied by the Soviet Union. GameCube received a port of that squad campaign.
tmnt: Ubisoft's TMNT adapts the 2007 CGI movie and lets the four brothers tag into combo strings during fights.
tom-clancys-rainbow-six-lockdown-2: Red Storm's Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six: Lockdown is the 2005 Rainbow Six that plays as a more linear shooter than the planning-heavy earlier games. GameCube is one of the console ports.
medal-of-honor-frontline: EA's Medal of Honor: Frontline is the 2002 World War II shooter that opens on the D-Day beach. The GameCube version followed the PlayStation 2 original.
harry-potter-and-the-goblet-of-fire: EA's Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire is the 2005 tie-in built around the Triwizard tasks. The GameCube version supports three players in those challenges.
sonic-heroes: Sonic Team's Sonic Heroes groups characters into speed, flight, and power teams in 2003. GameCube was a lead Nintendo version of that multiplatform platformer.
neighbours-from-hell-season-1: The German prank series about tormenting a noisy neighbor reached consoles as Neighbours from Hell: Revenge Is a Sweet Game. A GameCube version brings those trap-setting levels off the PC.
legacy-of-kain-blood-omen-2: Crystal Dynamics' Legacy of Kain: Blood Omen 2 continues Kain's vampire timeline in 2002 as a hack-and-slash sequel, years after the first Blood Omen.
spider-man-the-movie: Treyarch developed Activision's Spider-Man: The Movie, the 2002 tie-in to Sam Raimi's first film. The GameCube version is that 3D action game.
enter-the-matrix: Shiny Entertainment's Enter the Matrix sits beside The Matrix Reloaded and uses footage shot for the films. The 2003 GameCube version stars Niobe and Ghost.
resident-evil-zero: Capcom's Resident Evil Zero is a 2002 prequel made first for GameCube, pairing Rebecca Chambers with Billy Coen. A Wii edition later reissued that story.
fifa-street: EA Sports BIG's FIFA Street is a 2005 trick-based street soccer spinoff, not the annual simulation. GameCube was part of that original multiplatform release.
terraria: Re-Logic's Terraria is the 2011 sandbox of digging, crafting, and bosses, played on a flat plane. Ports reached Wii U, Nintendo 3DS, and Nintendo Switch.
assassins-creed-iv-black-flag: Ubisoft's Assassin’s Creed IV: Black Flag is the 2013 pirate story of Edward Kenway in the Caribbean. The Wii U version is a full release of that naval game.
super-meat-boy: Team Meat's Super Meat Boy is the 2010 platformer from Edmund McMillen and Tommy Refenes, a precise successor to the Flash game Meat Boy. Wii U and Switch ports followed the PC release.
minecraft: Markus Persson started Mojang's block-building sandbox Minecraft, publicly playable from 2009. Wii U, 3DS, and Switch editions are later ports of that world.
watch-dogs: Ubisoft's Watch Dogs is the 2014 open-world game about hacking Chicago's ctOS network. The Wii U port puts a map on the gamepad.
deus-ex-human-revolution-directors-cut: Eidos Montreal's expanded cyberpunk RPG Deus Ex: Human Revolution - Director's Cut launched on Wii U in 2013, restoring boss fights and adding commentary. Other platforms received that cut afterward.
assassins-creed-iii-2: Ubisoft's Assassin’s Creed III is the 2012 chapter set in the American Revolution, starring Connor. The Wii U port uses the gamepad for the map.
darksiders-warmastered-edition: The 2016 remaster of Vigil Games' horseman adventure is Darksiders Warmastered Edition, updating the 2010 original. Wii U and Nintendo Switch both received that edition.
dont-starve: Klei's Don't Starve is a 2013 wilderness survival game where hunger and darkness are the usual killers. The Wii U port is a console edition of that PC roguelike.
rayman-legends: Ubisoft's Rayman Legends followed Origins in 2013 and was shaped around the Wii U gamepad for Murfy's stages. A Nintendo Switch port later carried the same painted levels.
guacamelee-super-turbo-championship-edit: Drinkbox expanded its 2013 luchador adventure with extra stages on Wii U and Switch in Guacamelee! Super Turbo Championship Edition.
sniper-elite-v2: Rebellion's Sniper Elite V2 is the 2012 World War II sequel known for an X-ray bullet camera. A Wii U port brought those Berlin missions over.
bayonetta: Hideki Kamiya and PlatinumGames' Bayonetta is the 2009 character action game first published by Sega. Nintendo later funded Wii U and Switch ports, then a sequel.
cod-black-ops-ii: Treyarch's Call of Duty: Black Ops II splits its 2012 campaign between the 1980s and a near-future war. The Wii U version was a launch title, with loadouts on the gamepad.
the-binding-of-isaac-rebirth: Nicalis and Edmund McMillen rebuilt the 2011 roguelike as The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth in 2014. Wii U, 3DS, and Switch ports followed the PC release.
lego-the-hobbit: Traveller's Tales' LEGO The Hobbit is the 2014 brick telling of Peter Jackson's Hobbit films. Wii U and Nintendo 3DS were part of that release.
darksiders-ii: Vigil Games switched horsemen for Darksiders II in 2012, playing as Death and adding loot. Wii U and, later, Switch ports carry that action RPG.
child-of-light: Ubisoft Montreal's Child of Light is a 2014 role-playing fable told in rhyme, with a watercolor look. Wii U was an original platform, and Switch came later.
mass-effect-3: BioWare's Mass Effect 3 is the 2012 finale of Commander Shepard's trilogy. The Wii U version is a port that followed the Xbox 360, PlayStation 3, and PC releases.
the-swapper: Facepalm Games' The Swapper is a 2013 puzzle about making clones and moving your mind into them. The Wii U version ports that atmospheric PC game.
resident-evil-revelations-biohazard-reve: Capcom built Resident Evil Revelations first for the Nintendo 3DS in 2012, a cruise-ship story set between Resident Evil 4 and 5. Wii U and later Switch ports expanded it, Raid mode included.
never-alone: Upper One Games' Never Alone, also called Kisima Ingitchuna, is a 2014 puzzle platformer drawn from Inupiat folklore. Wii U and Switch versions include the cultural videos.
lego-marvel: Traveller's Tales' LEGO Marvel Super Heroes packs a large Marvel roster into an open New York in 2013, with Galactus among the threats.
steamworld-dig: Image & Form's mining adventure SteamWorld Dig first launched on the Nintendo 3DS eShop in 2013. Wii U and Switch ports followed that robot prospector.
thomas-was-alone: Mike Bithell's Thomas Was Alone is a 2012 puzzle about colored rectangles, narrated by Danny Wallace. Wii U and Switch ports came after the PC original.
scribblenauts-unlimited: 5th Cell's Scribblenauts Unlimited turns typed words into objects Maxwell can use, a 2012 puzzle. Wii U and Nintendo 3DS share that spawning trick.
race-the-sun: Flippfly's Race The Sun is a 2013 endless racer: a solar craft that fails when the sun sets. The Wii U version ports that minimalist PC game.
oddworld-new-n-tasty: Just Add Water's Oddworld: New 'n' Tasty rebuilds Abe's Oddysee in 2014, a new pass at the 1997 factory escape. Wii U was among the console releases.
call-of-duty-ghosts: Infinity Ward's Call of Duty: Ghosts is the 2013 shooter with a new cast after Modern Warfare. The Wii U version includes the campaign and uses the gamepad for extras.
sonic-all-stars-racing-transformed: Sumo Digital's Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed is a 2012 Sega crossover whose karts switch among car, boat, and plane in the middle of a lap.
how-to-survive: Eko Software's How to Survive is a 2013 zombie game about crafting weapons on an island. The Wii U port is a console edition of that overhead camp.
stealth-inc-2-game-of-clones: Curve Studios' Stealth Inc 2: A Game of Clones is a 2014 stealth-puzzle sequel, tied closely to the Wii U. Clones and light puzzles extend the test-chamber traps of the first game.
little-inferno: Tomorrow Corporation, the studio behind World of Goo, made Little Inferno in 2012: order toys from a catalog and burn them. The Wii U version was an early home for that fireplace.
lego-batman-3-beyond-gotham: Traveller's Tales sent the DC cast into space in LEGO Batman 3: Beyond Gotham, a 2014 sequel built around the Lantern Corps. Wii U and Nintendo 3DS were part of the release.
tom-clancys-splinter-cell-blacklist: Ubisoft's Tom Clancy’s Splinter Cell Blacklist is the 2013 Splinter Cell with a faster pace and a new voice for Sam Fisher. The Wii U version ports that campaign.
need-for-speed-most-wanted-a-criterion-g: Criterion's Need for Speed: Most Wanted - A Criterion Game is a 2012 open-city reboot, a different game from the 2005 Most Wanted. The Wii U version was part of that multiplatform release.
giana-sisters-twisted-dreams: Black Forest Games rebooted the 1987 platformer as Giana Sisters: Twisted Dreams in 2012, switching between dream worlds. A Wii U version brought that revival to Nintendo's console.
the-bridge: Gravity rotates around impossible architecture in The Bridge, a 2013 puzzle inspired by M.C. Escher. The Wii U release ports that black-and-white PC game.
fifa-2002: EA Sports released the soccer annual FIFA 2002 in 2001, with power-bar shooting. The GameCube version joined that year's multiplatform set.
sonic-adventure-2-battle: The GameCube edition of Sonic Adventure 2 is Sonic Adventure 2 Battle, adding more multiplayer to the hero and dark stories. It was a launch-window title for the console.
fifa-street-2: EA Sports BIG's FIFA Street 2 continues trick-based street soccer in 2006. The GameCube version arrived near the end of that console's sports lineup.
mario-party-7: Hudson and Nintendo's Mario Party 7 is the 2005 party game, the last Mario Party on GameCube. It supports eight players and the microphone accessory.
super-monkey-ball: Amusement Vision's Super Monkey Ball launched with the GameCube in 2001: tilt the stage to roll a monkey inside a ball. It grew out of the arcade Monkey Ball.
mario-party-6: Hudson's Mario Party 6 is the 2004 GameCube party game whose boards change on a day-and-night cycle. The microphone peripheral is used again.
nba-live-06: EA Sports' basketball annual NBA LIVE 06 shipped in 2005. The GameCube version is that season's edition of the long NBA Live series.
burnout: Criterion's Burnout started the series in 2001 around near-miss boosts and crashes. A GameCube port followed the PlayStation 2 original.
capcom-vs-snk-2: Capcom's 2001 crossover Capcom vs. SNK 2 mixes both companies' fighters under the groove system. The GameCube edition is the EO revision of that arcade game.
final-fantasy-crystal-chronicles: Square Enix's Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles is a 2003 GameCube action RPG built for four players linked to Game Boy Advances. It opened a spinoff line rather than continuing the numbered games.
harvest-moon-a-wonderful-life: Marvelous's Harvest Moon: A Wonderful Life follows one farmer across chapters of a life on GameCube. Natsume published the Western release that corresponds to the 2003 Japanese original.
james-bond-007-everything-or-nothing: EA's James Bond 007: Everything or Nothing is a 2004 third-person Bond game with Pierce Brosnan voicing 007. GameCube is one of the original releases.
the-lord-of-the-rings-the-third-age: EA's The Lord of the Rings: The Third Age is a 2004 role-playing game with an original party and turn-based battles running beside the film trilogy.
burnout-2-point-of-impact: Criterion's Burnout 2: Point of Impact adds a 2002 mode where the score comes from causing the biggest traffic pileup, alongside the usual races.
from-russia-with-love: EA's James Bond 007: From Russia with Love adapts the 1963 film in 2005 and uses Sean Connery's likeness, jetpack sequence included.
james-bond-007-agent-under-fire: EA's James Bond 007: Agent Under Fire is a 2001 original mission set, not adapted from one film. The GameCube version adds split-screen multiplayer the PlayStation 2 release lacked.
i-ninja: Argonaut's I-Ninja is a 2003 cartoon platformer about a small ninja grading his own combat. GameCube shipped with the PlayStation 2 and Xbox versions.
dragon-ball-z-budokai-2: Dimps' fighting sequel Dragon Ball Z: Budokai 2 adds fusions and a board-game story in 2003. The GameCube version is part of that multiplatform release, published by Atari in the West.
tom-clancys-rainbow-six-3-raven-shield: Red Storm's Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six 3: Raven Shield is the 2003 tactical shooter. The GameCube release is the action-led console edition, not the full PC mission planner.
star-fox-assault: Nintendo and Namco's Star Fox Assault (2005) sends Fox back to Arwing flights and on-foot shooting after Star Fox Adventures left the series on dinosaur-back. It is the GameCube entry, not Star Fox 64.
spyro-a-heros-tail: Eurocom took over Spyro for Spyro: A Hero's Tail in 2004, after Insomniac's trilogy, and Vivendi published that home-console sequel.
fifa-2003: EA Sports released FIFA 2003 in 2002, adding a Club Championship that pits licensed teams in a cup.
rock-band-2: Harmonix's Rock Band 2 is the 2008 instrument sequel, with a larger setlist and a tour mode. The Wii version supports the guitar, drums, and microphone.
check-vs-mate: Fantasy scenes play out the moves in Battle vs Chess, a 2011 chess game. Wii and Nintendo DS versions were released around that battle-chess idea.
metal-slug-2: SNK's METAL SLUG 2 is the 1998 run-and-gun sequel, adding transformations and new vehicles. A Wii release later reissued that Neo Geo game.
final-fantasy-iv: Square Enix's sequel to Final Fantasy IV, FINAL FANTASY IV: THE AFTER YEARS, follows a new generation after the original cast. It began on mobile phones and later reached Wii, DS, and 3DS.
sonic-unleashed: Sonic Team's Sonic Unleashed switches between daytime speed stages and a nighttime werehog in 2008. The Wii version was built separately from the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 game.
spider-man-3: Treyarch's Spider-Man 3 is the 2007 tie-in to Sam Raimi's third film, black suit included. The Wii version uses motion controls for that movie's action.
a-boy-and-his-blob: WayForward's A Boy and His Blob revives David Crane's 1989 puzzle in 2009: feed a blob to change its shape. Wii, DS, and 3DS all received that remake.
rock-band: Harmonix's Rock Band sold guitar, drums, and a microphone as one band kit in 2007. A Wii version followed the Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3 launch.
toy-story-3: Avalanche Software developed Disney's Disney•Pixar Toy Story 3: The Video Game in 2010, an open toy-box tie-in to the Pixar film. Wii and Nintendo DS versions both shipped.
the-amazing-spider-man: Beenox's The Amazing Spider-Man is the 2012 open-world game based on the Marc Webb film. Wii, Wii U, and the DS family received versions that differ from the main console release.
puzzle-quest: Infinite Interactive's Puzzle Quest: Challenge of the Warlords mixes match-three puzzles with a fantasy campaign in 2007, drawing on the Warlords line. Wii and Nintendo DS carried that board to consoles.
brothers-in-arms-road-to-hill-30: Gearbox opened its World War II squad line with Brothers in Arms: Road to Hill 30 (2005), a Normandy campaign in which giving orders mattered as much as the shooting.
fifa-11: EA Sports' club-season football sim FIFA 11 arrived in 2010, and the Wii edition kept motion swings while the other consoles stayed on a pad.
strong-bad-episode-4-dangeresque-3: Telltale put Strong Bad's homemade movie hero on a film set in Strong Bad's Cool Game for Attractive People: Episode 4 - Dangeresque 3: The Criminal Projective, a 2008 episode of the Homestar Runner series also sold on WiiWare.
strong-bad-episode-2-strong-badia-the-fr: Strong Bad tries to found a country in his own house in Strong Bad's Cool Game for Attractive People: Episode 2 - Strong Badia the Free, one of Telltale's 2008 Homestar Runner episodes on WiiWare.
strong-bad-episode-5-8-bit-is-enough: Retro games take over the season finale Strong Bad's Cool Game for Attractive People: Episode 5 - 8-Bit Is Enough, closing Telltale's 2008 Homestar Runner run, with a WiiWare release alongside PC.
spider-man-shattered-dimensions: Beenox split Spider-Man: Shattered Dimensions (2010) across four comic-book versions of the hero, while the Wii and DS releases are smaller cousins of that HD campaign.
