hyper-light-drifter: Heart Machine's wordless top-down action game Hyper Light Drifter, funded by a closely watched Kickstarter, was released in 2016.
dungeon-of-the-endless: Amplitude Studios mixed a dungeon crawl with tower defense in Dungeon of the Endless, a 2014 game set on a stranded crystal-powered ship.
tom-clancys-rainbow-six: Red Storm's 1998 tactical shooter Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six made players plan a breach, then carry it out, and a Nintendo 64 version followed.
mortal-kombat-trilogy: Midway packed the first three Mortal Kombat games into Mortal Kombat Trilogy in 1996. The Nintendo 64 cart held a larger roster than the PlayStation disc.
re-volt: Acclaim's 1999 remote-control racer Re-Volt runs toy cars through houses and streets, and the PC version includes a track editor.
conkers-bad-fur-day: Rare scrapped a family-friendly Conker game and shipped the foul-mouthed platformer Conker's Bad Fur Day instead, in 2001.
fighting-force: Core Design tried to carry belt-scrolling brawlers into 3D with Fighting Force, a 1997 beat-em-up on the new disc consoles and Nintendo 64.
pokemon-stadium-2: The Nintendo 64 battle game Pokémon Stadium 2 transfers Gold and Silver teams into 3D fights. Japan received it in 2000.
kirby-64-the-crystal-shards-2000: HAL Laboratory's Nintendo 64 platformer Kirby 64: The Crystal Shards, released in 2000, is the Kirby game where copied powers can be combined.
yoshis-story-1997: Nintendo followed Yoshi's Island with Yoshi's Story (1997), a side-scroller of pre-rendered scenery whose goal is collecting fruit.
mario-party-3: Hudson's Mario Party 3, released in 2000, added story duels and was the last Mario Party board game on the Nintendo 64.
mario-tennis-2000: Camelot's Nintendo 64 game Mario Tennis (2000) mixes tournament tennis with character growth, and a separate Game Boy Color game shares the name.
the-world-is-not-enough: Eurocom's Nintendo 64 first-person shooter 007: The World is not Enough, released in 2000, is a different game from the PlayStation tie-in to the same Bond film.
fifa-98-road-to-world-cup: EA themed its soccer annual around World Cup qualifying in FIFA '98: Road to World Cup, which shipped in 1997.
army-men-sarges-heroes: 3DO took the plastic army into a third-person shooter with Army Men: Sarge's Heroes in 1999, shrinking Sarge down into the human world.
destruction-derby: Reflections' 1995 combat racer Destruction Derby is about wrecking the other cars, and it became an early PlayStation staple.
nightmare-creatures: Kalisto's 1997 action game Nightmare Creatures is set in a monster-haunted London and plays as a weapon-based brawler.
mortal-kombat-mythologies-sub-zero: Midway stepped outside the tournaments with Mortal Kombat Mythologies: Sub-Zero in 1997, a side-scrolling prequel starring Sub-Zero.
robotron-2084: Eugene Jarvis and Larry DeMar's 1982 Williams arcade game Robotron: 2084 is the twin-stick shooter about saving the last humans from robots.
f-zero-x-1998: Nintendo EAD's 1998 futuristic racer F-Zero X puts a huge field of machines on the Nintendo 64 and is remembered for its speed and track design.
mario-golf-1999: Camelot's Nintendo 64 game Mario Golf (1999) pairs stroke play with a role-playing mode, beside a separate Game Boy Color version.
vigilante-8-2nd-offense: Luxoflux followed its vehicular combat game with Vigilante 8: 2nd Offense in 1999, still an alternate-1970s car war.
south-park-1998: Acclaim's first-person shooter South Park (1998), based on the Comedy Central show, was widely panned when it launched.
extreme-g-2: Acclaim's futuristic motorcycle sequel Extreme-G 2 arrived in 1998, continuing the anti-gravity bike races of the first game.
rampage-world-tour: Midway revived George, Lizzie, and Ralph for Rampage World Tour in 1997, a city-smashing sequel to the arcade monster game.
bomberman-64-1997: Hudson moved the series into polygonal stages with Bomberman 64 (1997), adding a single-player rescue story beside the blasting.
1080deg-snowboarding-1998: Nintendo EAD's weighty snowboard sim 1080° Snowboarding (N64) arrived in 1998 and stayed a favorite of the console's sports line.
gex-3-deep-cover-gecko: Crystal Dynamics closed its gecko trilogy with Gex 3: Deep Cover Gecko (1999), another platformer built on the character's TV-channel jokes.
jet-force-gemini: Rare's 1999 third-person shooter Jet Force Gemini stars a brother, a sister, and their dog against an insect army on the Nintendo 64.
harvest-moon-64-1999: Natsume's Nintendo 64 farm sim Harvest Moon 64 (1999) is about crops, livestock, and town life, a localization from the Bokujou Monogatari line.
international-superstar-soccer-64: Konami's International Superstar Soccer 64, released in 1997, was widely called the best soccer game on the Nintendo 64.
beetle-adventure-racing: Paradigm's 1999 arcade racer Beetle Adventure Racing uses Volkswagen's New Beetle and hides shortcuts in the scenery. Australia got it as HSV Adventure Racing.
space-station-silicon-valley: DMA Design's 1998 Space Station Silicon Valley lets the player possess robot animals while exploring a stranded station.
hey-you-pikachu: Nintendo's Hey You, Pikachu! uses the Nintendo 64 Voice Recognition Unit so a player can talk to Pikachu. The Japanese release was in 1998.
nba-live-2000: EA's annual basketball sim NBA Live 2000 shipped in 1999, covering the season that followed the lockout.
winback-covert-operations: Omega Force and Koei's 1999 third-person shooter Winback: Covert Operations is built around leaning out of cover, years before that style was common.
v-rally-1997: Infogrames' rally racer V-Rally (1997) helped establish the off-road series on PlayStation, with later ports and sequels under the same name.
wwf-no-mercy: AKI and THQ's 2000 wrestling game WWF No Mercy is still cited as a high point of the genre, especially its create-a-wrestler.
star-wars-episode-i-battle-for-naboo: Factor 5 followed Rogue Squadron with the Nintendo 64 flight shooter Star Wars Episode I: Battle for Naboo in 2000, this time from the Naboo side of the film.
chameleon-twist: Japan System Supply's 1997 platformer Chameleon Twist gives its hero a long tongue for swinging, swallowing, and reaching distant poles.
the-powerpuff-girls-chemical-x-traction: The Cartoon Network series became a 2001 fighter in The Powerpuff Girls: Chemical X-traction, with Chemical X as the power the title names.
custom-robo: Custom Robo is a toy-robot battler about outfitting a small fighter. The series began on the Nintendo 64 in Japan in 1999, and a GameCube game carried the short title west in 2004.
dr-mario-64: Nintendo brought the pill-matching puzzle to four players in Dr. Mario 64 in 2001, and the story mode puts Wario in the mix.
clayfighter-63-13: Interplay's claymation fighter ClayFighter 63⅓ arrived on the Nintendo 64 in 1997, a numbered sequel in the ClayFighter series.
mega-man-64-2001: Capcom's Mega Man 64 (2001) is the Nintendo 64 port of Mega Man Legends, the 3D adventure spinoff rather than a side-scrolling classic.
body-harvest: DMA Design's 1998 shooter Body Harvest, published by Gremlin, fights giant insects across several time periods in open areas.
superman-the-new-superman-adventures: Titus's 1999 Superman: The New Adventures, better known as Superman 64, is the Nintendo 64 game that became a fixture on worst-of lists.
cruisn-world: Midway followed Cruis'n USA with the globe-trotting arcade racer Cruis'n World in 1998.
bio-freaks: Midway's 1998 weapons fighter Bio F.R.E.A.K.S. lets combatants tear off limbs and bolt on replacements mid-battle.
south-park-chefs-luv-shack: Acclaim turned the Comedy Central show into a quiz-and-minigame party disc with South Park: Chef's Luv Shack in 1999, hosted by Chef.
snowboard-kids-2: Atlus's cartoon snowboard racer Snowboard Kids 2 arrived in 1999 as a sequel with new riders and courses.
power-rangers-lightspeed-rescue: The television season became a 2000 action game in Power Rangers Lightspeed Rescue, one of many licensed Power Rangers titles of that era.
nfl-blitz-1998: Midway's arcade football game NFL Blitz (1998) is known for late hits and exaggerated violence, not a league simulation.
ridge-racer-64: Nintendo Software Technology's 2000 Ridge Racer 64 is the Nintendo 64 chapter of Namco's series, built from Ridge Racer and Revolution courses.
road-rash-64: THQ's 1999 motorcycle brawler Road Rash 64 was made for the Nintendo 64 apart from Electronic Arts' earlier Road Rash games.
mission-impossible-1998: Ocean's stealth-action tie-in Mission: Impossible (1998) is based on the 1996 film and is best known in its Nintendo 64 version.
wcw-mayhem: Electronic Arts' 1999 WCW Mayhem is a professional wrestling game using the WCW license and its television roster.
turok-rage-wars: Acclaim's 1999 Turok: Rage Wars drops most of the exploration and focuses on multiplayer arena fights in the Turok setting.
nba-live-99: EA shipped the basketball annual NBA Live 99 in 1998, the edition tied to the lockout-shortened NBA season.
namco-museum-1995: PlayStation owners got Namco's arcade cabinet set in Namco Museum (1995), including Pac-Man, Galaga, Dig Dug, and other coin-op hits.
madden-nfl-2001: EA's football annual Madden NFL 2001 reached stores in 2000, part of the long Madden NFL series.
war-gods: Midway's 1996 3D weapon fighter War Gods used digitized characters, a follow-up in spirit to Mortal Kombat from the same publisher.
duke-nukem-64: Duke Nukem 64 is the cartridge port of Duke Nukem 3D, with violence trimmed for Nintendo and extra stages the PC release did not ship. The cartridge arrived in 1997.
international-track-field: Konami's button-mashing Olympic sequel International Track & Field 2000 is themed to the Sydney Games and follows the 1996 International Track & Field.
san-francisco-rush-2049: Atari pushed the arcade city racer into the future with San Francisco Rush 2049 in 2000, adding airborne and underground tracks.
rocket-robot-on-wheels: Sucker Punch's first game, the 1999 platformer Rocket: Robot on Wheels, showed off a physics-heavy Nintendo 64 engine before the studio moved on to Sly Cooper.
puzzle-bobble-2: Taito's bubble-matching sequel Puzzle Bobble 2, also widely sold as Bust-a-Move II, continues the aiming-and-matching puzzle of the arcade original.
wwf-war-zone: Acclaim's 1998 wrestling game WWF War Zone is remembered for a create-a-wrestler mode and full-motion entrances.
hot-wheels-turbo-racing: Stormfront Studios' 1999 Hot Wheels Turbo Racing is a Mattel-licensed arcade racer built around Hot Wheels cars.
nagano-winter-olympics-98: Konami's official licensed sports game Nagano Winter Olympics '98 shipped in 1997, with skiing, skating, and other winter events.
wipeout-64: Psygnosis brought anti-gravity racing to the Nintendo 64 with Wipeout 64 in 1998, an exclusive chapter of the Wipeout series.
iggys-reckin-balls: Iguana's 1998 party racer Iggy's Reckin' Balls rolls characters inside spiked balls through Nintendo 64 obstacle courses.
wwf-wrestlemania-2000: AKI and THQ's wrestling game WWF WrestleMania 2000 shipped in 1999 and set up the more celebrated No Mercy the following year.
madden-nfl-2002: EA's football annual Madden NFL 2002, released in 2001, was among the last Madden seasons published for the Nintendo 64.
wcw-nitro: Inland Productions and THQ's 1998 WCW Nitro is a wrestling game tied to the WCW Monday night television show.
san-francisco-rush-extreme-racing: Atari Games started the shortcut-filled city racer with San Francisco Rush: Extreme Racing in 1997.
international-superstar-soccer-2000: Konami continued its soccer series with International Superstar Soccer 2000, which reached the Nintendo 64 in 1999.
ms-pac-man-maze-madness: Namco's 2000 Ms. Pac-Man Maze Madness turns the dot-muncher into a 3D maze adventure instead of a straight arcade port.
cruisn-exotica: Midway's third Cruis'n arcade racer, Cruis'n Exotica, arrived in 2000 with fantasy courses beyond the earlier real-world tours.
puyo-puyo-sun: Compile's 1997 puzzle game Puyo Puyo SUN keeps the colored-blob chain clears and adds a sun meter that powers them up.
madden-nfl-2000: EA released the football annual Madden NFL 2000 in 1999, another season in the Madden NFL line.
mace-the-dark-age: Atari's 1997 weapons fighter Mace: The Dark Age pits fantasy combatants against each other in 3D arenas, in arcades and on the Nintendo 64.
chameleon-twist-2: Japan System Supply continued the tongue-swinging Nintendo 64 platformer with Chameleon Twist 2 in 1998.
nascar-2000: EA's stock-car annual NASCAR 2000 reached players in 1999, one entry in the long EA Sports NASCAR line.
monaco-grand-prix: Ubisoft's 1999 street-circuit racer Monaco Grand Prix focuses on the famous race around the principality and was also sold under a Racing Simulation name.
knockout-kings-2000: EA's licensed boxing game Knockout Kings 2000 shipped in 1999, part of the Knockout Kings series of real fighters.
wheel-of-fortune-old: Wheel of Fortune (Old) is an early home version of the television quiz show, dated 1988, in which players spin a wheel and call letters.
top-gear-rally: Boss Game Studios and Kemco's Nintendo 64 rally racer Top Gear Rally arrived in 1997, noted for changing weather on its courses.
puzzle-bobble-3: Taito's third bubble-matcher, Puzzle Bobble 3, continues the series also sold under the Bust-a-Move name.
wetrix: Zed Two's puzzle game Wetrix makes you raise and lower terrain so falling water does not spill off the map. It became a known Nintendo 64 puzzle release.
shadowgate-64-trials-of-the-four-towers: Kemco's 1999 Shadowgate 64: Trials of the Four Towers retells the 1987 castle adventure in 3D.
nascar-99: EA's stock-car annual NASCAR 99 shipped in 1998, an earlier season in the same NASCAR line as the later numbered editions.
ecw-hardcore-revolution: Acclaim's 2000 wrestling game ECW Hardcore Revolution uses the Extreme Championship Wrestling license and its hardcore-match reputation.
blues-brothers-2000: The platformer Blues Brothers 2000 follows Jake and Elwood and is tied to the film of the same name.
f-1-world-grand-prix: Video System's 1998 Nintendo 64 simulation F-1 World Grand Prix runs a Formula 1 season across real-world circuits.
battletanx-global-assault: 3DO followed its tank combat game with BattleTanx: Global Assault in 1999, another Nintendo 64 shooter of rival tanks.
buck-bumble: Argonaut's 1998 shooter Buck Bumble puts the player in control of an armed bee on the Nintendo 64.
automobili-lamborghini: Titus's 1997 Nintendo 64 racer Automobili Lamborghini is built around the Italian sports cars and was called Super Speed Race in Japan.
nba-hangtime: Midway's 1997 arcade basketball game NBA Hangtime succeeds NBA Jam, keeping the exaggerated dunks and adding a create-a-player.
polaris-snocross: Vicarious Visions' 2000 snowmobile racer Polaris SnoCross carries the Polaris brand onto the Nintendo 64.
hybrid-heaven: Konami's 1999 Nintendo 64 game Hybrid Heaven mixes role-playing stats with close-quarters fighting in a science-fiction setting.
aero-fighters-assault: Paradigm and Video System took the shooter series into 3D with Aero Fighters Assault, a 1997 Nintendo 64 entry.
scooby-doo-classic-creep-capers: THQ's 2001 Scooby-Doo! Classic Creep Capers is a 3D adventure based on the Hanna-Barbera cartoon and its mystery-solving crew.
pokemon-pinball: Jupiter and HAL Laboratory's 1999 Game Boy Color game Pokémon Pinball puts Pokemon on pinball tables and lets you catch them from the playfield.
102-dalmatians-puppies-to-the-rescue: The Disney film sequel got a 2000 platformer in 102 Dalmatians: Puppies to the Rescue, with puppies as the playable leads.
xena-warrior-princess: The syndicated television series received a 1999 PlayStation action game titled Xena: Warrior Princess. Titus later shipped a separate Game Boy Color version.
croc-2: Fox Interactive's 1999 platformer Croc 2 continues the crocodile adventure that began with Croc: Legend of the Gobbos.
army-men: 3DO opened its plastic-soldier line with Army Men in 1998, the green-versus-tan war that spawned a long run of sequels.
super-mario-bros-deluxe: Nintendo's 1999 Game Boy Color cart Super Mario Bros. Deluxe includes the original Super Mario Bros., Lost Levels material, and extra challenge modes.
x-men-mutant-academy: Activision's 2000 one-on-one fighter X-Men: Mutant Academy puts Marvel's mutant teams into versus matches.
metal-gear-ghost-babel: Konami's 2000 Game Boy Color game Metal Gear: Ghost Babel was retitled Metal Gear Solid outside Japan, but it tells a separate story from the PlayStation game.
blade: The Wesley Snipes vampire film received a handheld action tie-in in Blade (2000).
moorhuhn-2: The German casual hit about shooting pheasants gained a 2000 sequel in Moorhuhn 2, also known under the Crazy Chicken name.
lego-island-2-the-bricksters-revenge: LEGO Island 2: The Brickster's Revenge, released in 2001, continues the LEGO Island adventure after the Brickster's escape.
hugo-the-evil-mirror: The Danish TV-show troll returned in Hugo: The Evil Mirror, a 2002 platformer in the long Hugo series.
mat-hoffmans-pro-bmx: Activision's 2001 trick-biking game Mat Hoffman's Pro BMX carries the name of the real BMX rider, from the same boom as the Tony Hawk games.
mr-driller: Namco's 2000 puzzle game Mr. Driller sends the player drilling down through colored blocks while an air meter keeps running out.
test-drive-6: Accolade continued its street-racing series with Test Drive 6 in 1999, another set of licensed cars and point-to-point courses.
dave-mirra-freestyle-bmx: Acclaim's Dave Mirra Freestyle BMX, released in 2000, is the first game built around the X Games rider and other pro BMX tricks. The Game Boy Color cart is a smaller side-view edition, not the 3D PlayStation and Dreamcast game, and Dave Mirra Freestyle BMX 2 is the sequel.
buzz-lightyear-of-star-command: Disney's television spinoff, not the Toy Story films alone, is the source for Buzz Lightyear of Star Command, a 2000 platformer.
the-grinch: Ron Howard's film of the Dr. Seuss story got a 2000 platform tie-in simply titled The Grinch.
walt-disney-world-quest-magical-racing-t: Eidos published the 2000 kart racer Walt Disney World Quest: Magical Racing Tour, set in the Florida theme park.
chicken-run: Aardman's stop-motion film about chickens plotting an escape received a 2000 tie-in titled Chicken Run.
bust-a-move-4: Taito's fourth bubble-matcher, Puzzle Bobble 4, also sold as Bust-a-Move 4, continued the series on consoles in 1998.
wacky-races-1991: Hi-Tec Software's computer platformer Wacky Races (1991) is based on the Hanna-Barbera cartoon and appeared on machines such as the Amiga and Commodore 64.
hype-the-time-quest: Ubisoft's 1999 action RPG Hype: The Time Quest follows a knight thrown through time.
rampart-1990: Atari Games' arcade classic Rampart (1990) alternates building a castle wall with cannon defense, and it later spread to many home ports.
milons-secret-castle-1986: Hudson Soft's maze-like action game debuted on the Famicom Disk System in 1986 and reached the NES as Milon's Secret Castle (1988).
tomb-raider-curse-of-the-sword: Core Design made the 2001 Game Boy Color adventure Tomb Raider: Curse of the Sword, published by Activision as a sequel to the earlier handheld Tomb Raider.
lufia-the-legend-returns-2001: The Lufia series reached the Game Boy Color in Lufia: The Legend Returns (2001), a handheld role-playing continuation of that line.
stuart-little-2: The second Stuart Little film received a 2002 tie-in game titled Stuart Little 2.
survival-kids: Konami's 1999 Game Boy Color game Survival Kids, also called Stranded Kids, is about children living off a hostile island.
megami-tensei-gaiden-last-bible: Megami Tensei Gaiden: Last Bible is the Game Boy spinoff that opened the Last Bible line, a monster-collecting RPG under the Megami Tensei name.
harvest-moon-3-gbc-2000: Harvest Moon 3 GBC (2000) is the third color-handheld entry in the farming series, after Harvest Moon GB and Harvest Moon 2 GBC, about raising crops, animals, and town relationships.
redline-racer: Criterion Games' first release, the 1998 superbike racer Redline Racer, is an early step for the studio later known for Burnout.
warriors-of-might-and-magic: 3DO's 2000 Warriors of Might and Magic is an action role-playing spinoff, separate from the turn-based Heroes strategy games.
lego-stunt-rally: The brick-built racer LEGO Stunt Rally arrived in 2000, with tracks assembled from LEGO pieces.
woody-woodpecker-racing: Universal's cartoon bird headlines the 2000 kart racer Woody Woodpecker Racing, alongside other licensed characters.
deja-vu: ICOM Simulations' 1985 MacVenture Deja Vu: A Nightmare Comes True is a point-and-click noir mystery about an amnesiac in Chicago.
spider-man-n64: Marvel's wall-crawler headlines Spider-Man (2001), one of the action games from the wave of Spider-Man titles just before the 2002 film.
deer-hunter: The budget hunting sim Deer Hunter became a surprise PC hit in 1997 and later spun off a long line of follow-ups and ports.
spider-man-2-the-sinister-six: Torus Games' 2001 handheld Spider-Man 2: The Sinister Six pits the hero against that villain team, and it is not the later movie game.
wings-of-fury-1987: Broderbund's side-scrolling World War II game Wings of Fury (1987) launches the player from a carrier to strafe ships and ground targets.
alleyway: Nintendo's 1989 Game Boy launch-window game Alleyway is a brick-breaker starring Mario, in the tradition of Breakout.
earthworm-jim-menace-2-the-galaxy: Crave and IMS Productions' 1999 handheld platformer Earthworm Jim: Menace 2 the Galaxy is a later, smaller entry in the Earthworm Jim series.
toobin: Atari Games' 1988 arcade game Toobin' sends riders down a river on inner tubes, dodging hazards and tossing cans at obstacles.
pokemon-trading-card-game-2: The Japanese Game Boy Color sequel Pokemon Trading Card Game 2 arrived in 2001 and did not get an official English release at the time.
harry-potter-and-the-sorcerers-stone-200: Griptonite's 2001 Game Boy Color RPG Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (GBC) adapts the first story and is separate from the console action games.
new-york-race: Kalisto's 2001 futuristic racer New York Race began as a Fifth Element game and shipped without that film's license.
titus-the-fox-1991: Titus the Fox (GB, GBC) is the handheld port of the platformer about a fox heading for Marrakech. The computer original is from 1992, and the Game Boy edition followed in 1993.
star-wars-yoda-stories: LucasArts' 1997 desktop game Star Wars: Yoda Stories builds a short randomized adventure around Yoda each time it is played.
shin-megami-tensei-devil-children: Atlus aimed Shin Megami Tensei: Devil Children at a younger audience in 2000, a Game Boy Color spinoff that pairs children with demon partners.
lego-alpha-team: The PC puzzle adventure LEGO Alpha Team arrived in 2000, with agents taking apart the Brickster's contraptions.
shin-megami-tensei-devil-children-black-: Atlus sold Shin Megami Tensei: Devil Children: Black Book in 2000 as one of two paired Game Boy Color cartridges, alongside a Red Book with its own path.
shamus-1982: William Mataga's maze shooter Shamus (1982), published by Synapse, was an Atari 8-bit favorite about a detective in a robot-filled labyrinth.
batman-chaos-in-gotham: DC's hero headlines the 2001 handheld action game Batman: Chaos in Gotham, drawn from the animated-series era of Batman licenses.
suzuki-alstare-extreme-racing: The motorcycle team license shows up in Suzuki Alstare Extreme Racing, a 1999 bike racer.
shanghai: Activision published Brodie Lockard's Shanghai in 1986, the mahjong-solitaire game about clearing matching tiles from a stacked layout.
dropzone-1984: Archer MacLean's single-screen shooter Dropzone (1984) follows the Defender tradition and became a favorite on 8-bit Atari computers.
the-black-onyx: Henk Rogers' 1984 computer RPG The Black Onyx is often credited as the commercial role-playing game that opened Japan's home-computer market to the genre.
disneys-atlantis-the-lost-empire-the-los: Disney's animated film received a 2001 action tie-in in Disney's Atlantis: The Lost Empire.
balloon-kid-1990: Nintendo's Game Boy follow-up to Balloon Fight, Balloon Kid (1990), stars Alice as she stays aloft with the balloons she carries.
nicktoons-racing: Several Nickelodeon cartoons share the tracks in Nicktoons Racing, a 1999 kart racer.
magical-drop: Data East's 1995 puzzle game Magical Drop has the player catch falling drops and throw them back to clear columns of color.
quest-for-camelot: Warner Bros.' animated film received a 1998 action tie-in titled Quest for Camelot.
shadowgate-classic: ICOM's 1987 MacVenture Shadowgate Classic is the point-and-click castle adventure that later traveled to many home computers and handhelds.
harry-potter-and-the-chamber-of-secrets-: Griptonite followed its first handheld RPG with Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (GBC) in 2002, again separate from the console action game.
star-ocean-blue-sphere: tri-Ace and Enix released Star Ocean: Blue Sphere only in Japan, in 2001, as a Game Boy Color follow-up set after Star Ocean: The Second Story.
the-dukes-of-hazzard: The Dukes of Hazzard is a video game based on the CBS series about cousins Bo and Luke Duke and their car, the General Lee.
lego-alpha-team-2001: Lego Alpha Team (2001) is the handheld puzzle game starring those agents, and it plays differently from the PC adventure released the year before.
pokemon-gold-version: Game Freak's Pokémon Gold Version opened the Johto generation on the Game Boy Color, in Japan in 1999 and in the West in 2000.
xtreme-sports-2000: WayForward packed several extreme-sports events into the Game Boy Color game Xtreme Sports (2000).
pocket-bomberman: Hudson's 1997 Pocket Bomberman turns Bomberman into a side-scrolling platformer instead of a maze battle.
oddworld: The 2001 handheld follow-up Oddworld Adventures 2 draws on Abe's Exoddus for the Game Boy Color.
x-men-mutant-wars: Marvel's mutants appear in the 2000 side-scrolling action game X-Men: Mutant Wars, a different title from the one-on-one Mutant Academy fighter.
x-men-wolverines-rage: Wolverine carries the 2001 handheld action game X-Men: Wolverine's Rage, another Marvel license aimed at the Game Boy Color.
spongebob-squarepants-legend-of-the-lost: One of the earliest games from the Nickelodeon cartoon, SpongeBob SquarePants: Legend of the Lost Spatula is a 2001 Game Boy Color platformer.
hamtaro-ham-hams-unite: The hamster cartoon reached the Game Boy Color in Hamtaro Ham-Hams Unite!, which came west in 2001.
pong-the-next-level: Hasbro updated the 1972 paddle game with power-ups in Pong: The Next Level, released in 1999.
game-watch-gallery-2: Nintendo's second Game & Watch collection, Game & Watch Gallery 2, pairs the old LCD modes with redrawn versions starring Mario characters. The color edition arrived in 1998.
legend-of-zelda-links-awakening-dx: The 1998 color update Legend Of Zelda: Link's Awakening DX rebuilds the 1993 Game Boy adventure with color, a photo feature, and an extra Color Dungeon.
microsoft-pinball-arcade: Microsoft's 1998 collection Microsoft Pinball Arcade recreates a set of real pinball tables for play at home.
shin-megami-tensei-devil-children-red-bo: The companion cartridge Shin Megami Tensei: Devil Children: Red Book shipped in 2000 beside Black Book, the other half of Atlus's paired Devil Children release.
conkers-pocket-tales: Rare's 1999 Game Boy Color adventure Conker's Pocket Tales stars a gentle Conker, made before the adult humor of Bad Fur Day.
ronaldo-v-football: Infogrames' 2000 soccer game Ronaldo V-Football is endorsed by the Brazilian striker Ronaldo, and it is also known as Ronaldo V-Soccer in the United States.
ultimate-fighting-championship: The mixed-martial-arts promotion lent its name to Ultimate Fighting Championship, an early licensed fighting game from 2000.
resident-evil-code-veronica: Capcom's 2000 Dreamcast game Resident Evil Code: Veronica follows Claire Redfield and is a mainline entry, even though it sits outside the numbered titles.
army-men-rts: The plastic soldiers moved into real-time strategy with Army Men RTS in 2002, commanding Sarge's troops across oversized household battlefields.
disneypixar-cars-2: THQ's 2006 racing game Disney•Pixar Cars is the tie-in to the first Pixar film, not to the later Cars sequel.
worms-3d: Team17 took the artillery series fully into 3D with Worms 3D in 2003, leaving the familiar side-on battlefield.
true-crime-streets-of-la: Luxoflux's 2003 open-world game True Crime: Streets of LA stars cop Nick Kang in Los Angeles, with a meter that tracks whether he stays clean.
second-sight: Free Radical Design, the TimeSplitters studio, released the psychic action game Second Sight in 2004.
true-crime-new-york-city: Luxoflux moved the open-world cop series to Manhattan with True Crime: New York City in 2005, starring Marcus Reed.
tony-hawks-american-wasteland: Neversoft set Tony Hawk's American Wasteland in Los Angeles in 2005 and linked its skate areas into one continuous city.
sonic-3d-blast-1996: Traveller's Tales put Sonic in an isometric view for Sonic 3D Blast (1996), a Genesis game that also shipped on the Saturn.
metal-gear-solid-the-twin-snakes: Silicon Knights remade the 1998 stealth game as Metal Gear Solid: The Twin Snakes on the GameCube in 2004, with new cutscenes directed by Ryuhei Kitamura.
crash-bandicoot-wrath-of-cortex: Traveller's Tales' 2001 platformer Crash Bandicoot: The Wrath of Cortex is the fourth main Crash game and introduces the brute Crunch.
sonic-riders: Sonic Team replaced footraces with hoverboard Extreme Gear in Sonic Riders, the 2006 racing game.
shadow-the-hedgehog: Sega gave the black hedgehog guns and a branching hero-or-villain story in Shadow the Hedgehog, released in 2005.
def-jam-fight-for-ny: AKI and EA's 2004 hip-hop fighter Def Jam: Fight for NY is the sequel to Def Jam Vendetta, with a roster full of rappers.
the-legend-of-zelda-four-swords-adventur: Nintendo's 2004 GameCube game The Legend of Zelda: Four Swords Adventures is a multiplayer Zelda that links Game Boy Advance systems for four players.
call-of-duty-finest-hour: Spark Unlimited brought the World War II shooter to consoles for the first time with Call of Duty: Finest Hour in 2004.
mortal-kombat-deception: Midway followed Deadly Alliance with Mortal Kombat: Deception in 2004, adding Chess Kombat and a puzzle mode beside the fights.
timesplitters-2: Free Radical's 2002 shooter TimeSplitters 2 is remembered for time-hopping missions, a map maker, and strong multiplayer.
x-men-legends-2-rise-of-apocalypse: Raven Software's squad action RPG X-Men Legends II: Rise of Apocalypse, published by Activision in 2005, is the sequel to X-Men Legends.
skies-of-arcadia: Overworks' 2000 Dreamcast RPG Skies of Arcadia follows air pirates among floating islands, and a later GameCube edition was titled Legends.
tales-of-symphonia-2003: Namco's GameCube action RPG Tales of Symphonia (2003) follows Lloyd Irving and uses the series' real-time battles. It was a console exclusive at launch.
timesplitters-future-perfect: Free Radical closed the trilogy with TimeSplitters: Future Perfect in 2005, adding a four-player campaign and console online play.
resident-evil-code-veronica-x-2: The expanded edition Resident Evil - Code: Veronica X adds scenes to Code Veronica. It spread widely on PlayStation 2 in 2001 and later reached the GameCube.
sonic-spinball-1993: Sega turned Sonic into a set of flipper tables with Sonic Spinball (1993), a Genesis pinball game built around his speed.
call-of-duty-2-big-red-one: Treyarch's 2005 console shooter Call of Duty 2: Big Red One follows the U.S. 1st Infantry Division and was not a PC expansion.
hulk: Radical Entertainment's 2003 film tie-in The Hulk switches between rampaging as the creature and playing as Banner.
crash-tag-team-racing: Radical Entertainment's 2005 Crash Tag Team Racing mixes karts with on-foot platforming, and cars can fuse in the middle of a race.
ssx-3: EA Canada's 2003 snowboard game SSX 3 puts the series on one connected mountain instead of a menu of separate courses.
mario-party-4: Hudson's Mario Party 4, released in 2002, was the first Mario Party on the GameCube and kept the boards-and-minigames format.
star-fox-adventures: Rare's 2002 GameCube game Star Fox Adventures began as the separate project Dinosaur Planet before it was recast around Fox McCloud.
viewtiful-joe-2003: Clover Studio and Hideki Kamiya's side-scroller Viewtiful Joe (2003) gives its hero film-style VFX powers on the GameCube.
teenage-mutant-ninja-turtles-mutant-mele: Konami's 2005 arena brawler Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Mutant Melee is a fighting spinoff of the cartoons, not a story platformer.
spyro-enter-the-dragonfly: After Insomniac left the series, Spyro: Enter the Dragonfly arrived in 2002 under Universal and launched to a notoriously rough reception.
medal-of-honor-rising-sun-2003: EA moved Medal of Honor from Europe to the Pacific theater with Medal of Honor: Rising Sun in 2003.
hobbit-the-2003: Sierra's action game based on Tolkien's novel shipped as Hobbit, The (2003), a tie-in era adaptation rather than a later film game.
mario-party-5: Hudson stayed on the GameCube for Mario Party 5 in 2003, another board-and-minigame party with a new set of boards.
barnyard: Nickelodeon's animated film about a farm of animals received a 2006 tie-in game titled Barnyard.
mario-power-tennis: Camelot added charged special shots to the Mario tennis formula in Mario Power Tennis, a 2004 GameCube game.
ice-age-2-the-meltdown: The Blue Sky film sequel received a 2006 platform tie-in titled Ice Age 2: The Meltdown.
medal-of-honor-european-assault: EA returned Medal of Honor to the European theater with Medal of Honor: European Assault in 2005, after the Pacific-set Rising Sun.
dragon-ball-z-budokai: Dimps opened its long line of 3D anime fighters with Dragon Ball Z: Budokai in 2002.
driver-san-francisco: Ubisoft Reflections built Driver San Francisco in 2011 around Shift, a power that jumps the player from car to car across an open city.
alone-in-the-dark: Eden Games rebooted the survival-horror series with Alone in the Dark (2008), moving the story to Central Park and splitting the game into episodes.
sonic-the-hedgehog-4-episode-1: Dimps and Sonic Team returned to side-view Sonic in 2010 with Sonic the Hedgehog 4 - Episode I, sold as an episodic follow-up to the Genesis games.
metal-slug-x: SNK's 1999 Metal Slug X revises Metal Slug 2, rebalancing the run-and-gun and easing the slowdown that hurt the earlier board.
metal-slug: Nazca's 1996 Neo Geo run-and-gun METAL SLUG launched the series, with chunky vehicles and a small squad against General Morden's army.
sega-bass-fishing: The 2008 Wii release SEGA Bass Fishing brings Sega's arcade fishing game, originally Get Bass, to motion controls.
call-of-duty-3: Treyarch's 2006 World War II shooter Call of Duty 3 was built for consoles and did not receive a PC version at launch.
la-mulana: Nigoro's ruin explorer La-Mulana homages MSX action adventures. It began as 2005 freeware, and a remake reached more players around 2012.
bittrip-beat: Gaijin Games opened the BIT.TRIP series on WiiWare in 2009 with BIT.TRIP BEAT, a rhythm game in which CommanderVideo bounces a dot to the beat.
destroy-all-humans: Pandemic's 2005 Destroy All Humans! casts the alien Crypto as a 1950s invader harvesting human brains.
fifa-10: EA Sports shipped the annual soccer game FIFA 10 in 2009, another season in the long-running FIFA series on consoles and PC.
tales-of-monkey-island-complete-pack-cha: Telltale's second episode, Tales of Monkey Island Complete Pack: Chapter 2 - The Siege of Spinner Cay, strands Guybrush on the merfolk island of Spinner Cay while the Pox of LeChuck from the 2009 season keeps spreading. It is one WiiWare chapter of that five-part revival, not a LucasArts Monkey Island.
Third of five episodes in Telltale's 2009 season, Tales of Monkey Island Complete Pack: Chapter 3 - Lair of the Leviathan keeps Guybrush Threepwood as the pirate lead.
Telltale closed its five-episode 2009 Monkey Island season with Tales of Monkey Island Complete Pack: Chapter 5 - Rise of the Pirate God.
Fourth in Telltale's 2009 run, Tales of Monkey Island Complete Pack: Chapter 4 - The Trial and Execution of Guybrush Threepwood puts the series hero's name on the episode itself.
ori-and-the-will-of-the-wisps: Moon Studios followed its hand-painted platformer with Ori and the Will of the Wisps in 2020, again published with Microsoft.
hotline-miami-2-wrong-number: Dennaton's top-down sequel Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number arrived in 2015, larger and more divisive than the 2012 original.
resident-evil-6: Capcom pushed the series toward action in Resident Evil 6 in 2012, splitting the story across campaigns for Leon, Chris, Jake, and Ada.
grim-fandango-remastered: Double Fine's 2015 Grim Fandango Remastered updates Tim Schafer's 1998 LucasArts adventure about a travel agent in the Land of the Dead.
the-outer-worlds: Obsidian's satirical first-person RPG The Outer Worlds, published by Private Division in 2019, is set in the corporately owned Halcyon colony.
broforce: Free Lives' run-and-gun Broforce, published by Devolver Digital in 2015, parodies action movies by making each bro a send-up of a film hero.
the-walking-dead-season-2: Telltale continued its comic-based adventure with The Walking Dead: Season 2 in 2013, this time with Clementine as the lead.
borderlands-3: Gearbox continued the looter-shooter series with Borderlands 3 in 2019, introducing a new group of vault hunters.
syberia-2: Benoit Sokal's 2004 adventure Syberia 2 continues Kate Walker's journey with Hans Voralberg, the sequel to the 2002 game.
celeste: Maddy Thorson and Noel Berry's 2018 platformer Celeste sends Madeline up a mountain and was praised for its assist options as much as its precision.
to-the-moon: Kan Gao and Freebird Games released To the Moon in 2011, an RPG Maker story about granting a dying man's wish by editing his memories.
frostpunk: 11 bit studios' 2018 city builder Frostpunk is about keeping the last settlement alive around a generator in an endless winter.
smite: Hi-Rez's free-to-play battleground SMITE pits gods from world myth against each other in a third-person lane fight, and it left beta for a full release in 2015.
borderlands-game-of-the-year-enhanced: Gearbox's 2009 looter shooter returned as Borderlands Game of the Year Enhanced in 2019, with updated visuals and a handful of gameplay additions.
batman-arkham-asylum: Rocksteady started the Arkham series with Batman: Arkham Asylum in 2009, a stealth-action game set inside the asylum and written with Paul Dini.
dead-by-daylight: Behaviour Interactive's 2016 asymmetric horror game Dead by Daylight pits four survivors against one killer.
overcooked: Ghost Town Games' co-op kitchen game Overcooked, published by Team17 in 2016, is about cooking under a timer as the kitchen falls apart.
stalker-shadow-of-chernobyl: GSC Game World opened its series with S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Shadow of Chernobyl in 2007, a first-person survival shooter in the Zone around the Chernobyl plant.
human-fall-flat: No Brakes Games' 2016 physics puzzle Human: Fall Flat stars a wobbly human figure and later became a popular co-op party game.
the-long-dark: Hinterland's Canadian wilderness survival game The Long Dark entered early access in 2014, with its story mode arriving later.
stray-2: BlueTwelve Studio's 2022 Stray, published by Annapurna Interactive, follows a cat through a sealed city inhabited by robots.
mortal-kombat-11: NetherRealm's 2019 fighter Mortal Kombat 11 emphasizes custom move sets and a roster that mixes series regulars with guest characters.
dark-souls8482-remastered: FromSoftware's 2011 action RPG returned as Dark Souls: Remastered in 2018, including the Artorias of the Abyss content.
it-takes-two-2: Hazelight and Josef Fares made the co-op-only platformer It Takes Two in 2021, and it won Game of the Year at The Game Awards.
darksiders-ii-deathinitive-edition: The 2015 enhanced rerelease Darksiders II Deathinitive Edition updates the 2012 sequel, which shifts the horseman lead from War to Death.
kotor-ii: Obsidian's 2004 sequel Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II – The Sith Lords followed BioWare's RPG and is famous for a rushed launch later patched by fans.
beholder: Warm Lamp Games' 2016 Beholder makes you a landlord in a totalitarian state, ordered to spy on the tenants of your building.
prison-architect-all-day-and-a-psych: Introversion's prison-management sim Prison Architect reached a full 1.0 release in 2015 after a long public alpha.
resident-evil-2-2019: Capcom's 2019 Resident Evil 2 is the over-the-shoulder remake of the 1998 survival-horror game, again following Leon and Claire.
jotun: Thunder Lotus Games' hand-painted boss battles against Norse giants were packaged as Jotun: Valhalla Edition, the complete form of the 2015 game.
trine-enchanted-edition: Trine Enchanted Edition refreshes Frozenbyte's 2009 puzzle platformer, in which a thief, a wizard, and a knight combine their skills.
enter-the-gungeon: Dodge Roll's bullet-hell roguelike Enter the Gungeon, published by Devolver Digital in 2016, is set in a dungeon full of guns.
re-revelations-2: Capcom released Resident Evil Revelations 2 in episodes in 2015, pairing Claire Redfield with Barry Burton.
resident-evil-3: Capcom's 2020 Resident Evil 3 reimagines the 1999 Nemesis story with Jill Valentine, as a shorter companion to the second game's remake.
fornite-battle-royale: Epic Games launched the free 100-player mode Fortnite Battle Royale in 2017, and it quickly overshadowed the original Save the World campaign.
mark-of-the-ninja: Klei's 2012 side-view stealth game Mark of the Ninja shows sound and light so the player can plan each takedown.
